a14-0000025.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000025.text: Shepard reports roll program completed. Pitch profiles still in progress. 37 seconds.

a14-0000025.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0000025.text: Stand by for Mode One Bravo.

a14-0000025.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000025.text: CapCom Gordon Fullerton making that report.

a14-0000025.speaker: Shepard
a14-0000025.text: Okay. Coming up on our favorite number, babe.

a14-0000025.speaker: Roosa
a14-0000025.text: Stand by. I didn't want you to - I was going to give you that one.

a14-0000025.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000025.text: Cabin pressure coming down. Adjusting from sea level to the space environment.

a14-0000025.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000025.text: Status check in Mission Control coming up all greens on the Flight Director's console.

a14-0000025.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0000025.text: 14, Houston. Everything looks good here on the ground.

a14-0000025.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000025.text: One minute, 19 seconds; coming up on period of maximum aerodynamic pressure on the vehicle.

a14-0000025.speaker: Shepard
a14-0000025.text: And we got through Max Q real fine, troops.

a14-0000025.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000025.text: One minute, 35 seconds and 9 nautical miles [17 km] in altitude, 5 nautical miles [9 km] downrange. The velocity now reading 3,340 feet per second [1,018 m/s].

a14-0000025.speaker: Shepard
a14-0000025.text: Now, we're off and running. Look at the ice coming off.

a14-0000025.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0000025.text: Stand by for Mode One Charlie.

a14-0000025.speaker: Shepard
a14-0000025.text: We're One Charlie. EDS Auto's Off.

a14-0000025.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000025.text: 2 minutes, 5 seconds. Coming up on center engine shutdown.

a14-0000025.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000025.text: 2 minutes, 12 seconds; 20 nautical miles [37 km] in altitude.

a14-0000025.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000025.text: 2 minutes, 25 seconds; 25 nautical miles [46 km] in altitude, 30 nautical miles [56 km] downrange.

a14-0000025.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000025.text: Mark. 2 minutes, 35 seconds. Coming up on staging.

a14-0000244.speaker: Roosa
a14-0000244.text: Okay. You could see the flare from lift-off.

a14-0000244.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000244.text: Had staging. The Shepard crew now riding on five good second stage engines.

a14-0000244.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0000244.text: Roger. We confirm good thrust on all five. [Long pause.]

a14-0000244.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000244.text: The giant first stage falling away now. It's day's work done. Three minutes, 10 seconds; coming up on skirt sep and tower jettison.

a14-0000244.speaker: Roosa
a14-0000244.text: If we don't get that job...

a14-0000244.speaker: Roosa
a14-0000244.text: ...We're about 4 seconds from S-II Sep. Right.

a14-0000244.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000244.text: The Launch Escape Tower has ejected on time.

a14-0000244.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0000244.text: Roger. We confirm the skirt Sep. And you're in Mode II now.

a14-0000244.speaker: Roosa
a14-0000244.text: We're in Mode II in the cockpit, troops.

a14-0000244.speaker: Shepard
a14-0000244.text: ...Pitch to Rate - Pitch to Rate Command Delta V C .

a14-0000244.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000244.text: Three minutes, 35 seconds; 14 now 33 feet [10 m] shorter; 9,000 pounds [4 tons] lighter; moving out well beyond the Earth's atmosphere. We show an altitude of 60 nautical miles [111 km].

a14-0000244.speaker: Roosa
a14-0000244.text: Better watch this; that horizon is beautiful.

a14-0000244.speaker: Shepard
a14-0000244.text: Keep your eyes on the pin, cockpit troops.

a14-0000244.speaker: Roosa
a14-0000244.text: Yes. Okay, we're coming up toward 4 minutes. We're pitching 42.6; it looks real good, leader.

a14-0000244.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000244.text: Mark; 3 minutes, 55 seconds; 63 nautical miles [117 km] in altitude. 143 nautical miles [265 km] downrange. Velocity now...

a14-0000244.speaker: Roosa
a14-0000244.text: And that center engine is burning.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: 14, Houston. At 4 minutes, trajectory and guidance look good.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Okay, 4 minutes, 6 [garble]...

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: 14; Roger.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Right smack dab in the money.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Beautiful.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Just smack dab in...

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: And, 14; Houston. The CMC is Go.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Roger; CMC , Go.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Four minutes, 20 seconds; velocity now reading 10,750 feet per second [3,277 m/s] and accelerating. In Mission Control, Apollo 14's trajectory data driving right down the middle of our plot boards. Right now flight path data is Go.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: We're about 50 miles, Ed.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Oh, great. Everything's Go on this side, Al.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Good show, buddy.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Okay.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: 04:30. 73.5. We are absolutely beautiful. It is right in the fracking money. There's a little more ice flaking off.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Okay. We're still upstaging for three-on program at this point.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: We don't have S-IVB ...

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: No, we don't. No, we don't. That's right. COI 's 5:45, not 4:45.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Coming up on five minutes, 78 nautical miles [144 km] in altitude, 235 nautical miles [435 km] downrange.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Retrofire also reports there - 14 is clear of the Atlantic weather.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: And at 5 minutes. Eighty miles. We're riding within two or three tenths of - of this profile. Beautiful.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Just can't beat it, huh?

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Smooth. Just looks like a little side oscillation in the couch.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: That's all you're feeling; just like a railroad coach is this couch.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Okay, 5 plus 20; we should have COI here in 25 seconds.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: [garble] 25 seconds. About 13 2, 8 26...

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Predicted time for S-II shutdown; 9 minutes, 16 seconds. Very close to normal. We're at five minutes, 45 seconds.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Stand by for S-IVB to COI .

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Mark. S-IVB to COI now.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: S-IVB to COI .

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Okay, Ed, babe, stand by for the gimbal motors.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Roger. And your times are nominal. Level sense arm, 8 plus 39, and S-II cut-off at 9 plus 16.

a14-t-0000400-cm.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0000400-cm.text: Gimbal motors...

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000600.text: Okay. GPI . Verify a minus 145 and plus 130.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000600.text: CapCom Gordon Fullerton reporting that 14 capable of reaching the minimum orbit with the combination of a good third stage and Service Module engines. Meanwhile in Mission Control, a status check being taken. Coming up all greens. We're at 6 minutes, 20 seconds; 1,491 nautical miles [2,761 km]...

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000600.text: At 6:30. I think we got TLI , now, on that center engine, no matter what.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000600.text: Six minutes, 30 seconds; 93 nautical [172 km] in altitude; 420 nautical miles [778 km] downrange.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000600.text: ...about 2 and a fourth before nominal here. The heat's still going.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0000600.text: Stand by for S-IVB to orbit.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0000600.text: Mark. You have S-IVB to orbit now.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000600.text: And it's beautiful. This trajectory is absolutely fantastic.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000600.text: Shepard, Roosa, Mitchell now told that they can reach orbit on booster power only if given a good third stage. Six minutes, 55 seconds; 95 nautical miles [176 km] in altitude.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000600.text: Seven minutes, 5 seconds and 499 nautical miles [924 km] downrange. Velocity now reading 16,587 feet per second [5,056 m/s].

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000600.text: Okay. We got about 45 seconds now. [Garble] nominally.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000600.text: This guidance is steady as a rock.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000600.text: We are right in the numbers. Just right - [garble] seems like there's something I ought to be doing. Strike 20 seconds from the board. [Garble] now.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000600.text: Seven minutes, 30 seconds; 14 flying almost parallel over the ocean now with Shepard - with the Shepard crew in a heads-down position. Really moving out now for downrange distance. We show downrange of 587 nautical miles [1,087 km].

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000600.text: That was center engine shut down right on time. Good thrust on the other four.

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000600.text: Hey, did you feel that PU valve?

a14-t-0000600.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000600.text: Yes. Sure did. Didn't hear it though.

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: Well, I - I had to give you noise from the simulator. Good. Can't give you everything. We're within 2/10ths in altitude. Just right down the money.

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: Eight minutes, 10 seconds of 14; now 98 nautical miles [181 km] in altitude, 700 nautical miles [1,296 km] downrange. Velocity now reading 19,881 feet per second [6,060 m/s]. Staging status...

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: About 20 seconds to level sense arm.

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: 14, Houston. You're Go for staging. The CMC is Go.

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: Just a little high, but it's bringing the H-dot down. Just a little vibration about [garble]...

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: You have level sense arm now.

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: Very slight pogo and starting at 8:40.

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: Time hack. You ought to be pretty close to Mode IV.

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: Mark; 9 minutes, 100 nautical miles [185 km] in altitude, 830 nautical miles [1,537 km] downrange.

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: Just a little high. We're about a mile high. It ought...

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: Stand by for a Mode IV capability.

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: That Mode 4 call says a good Serv...

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: Look at the ice go up there.

a14-t-0000802-hold12.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0000802-hold12.text: 9 minutes, 30 seconds. Thrust looks good on the S-IVB after staging.

a14-0000930.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0000930.text: 14, Houston. Thrust looks good on the S-IVB .

a14-0000930.speaker: Roosa
a14-0000930.text: Okay. Okay. We're at 101.3 and it's bringing the H-dot down. Starting our run now.

a14-0000930.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0000930.text: The Shepard crew has now used up two thirds of their Saturn stages on their way to orbit. We're at 9 minutes, 45 seconds. 101 nautical miles [187 km] in altitude. 989 nautical miles [1,832 km] downrange. Velocity now reading at twenty three thousand, three hun... - 23,313 feet per second [7,106 m/s].

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0001000.text: H-dot is just about zero. We're 102...

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0001000.text: 10 minutes, 25 seconds. 102 nautical miles [189 km] in al - altitude. Eleven thousand, four hundred and forty three nautical miles [means 1,143, 2,117 km] downrange. Velocity now reading 24,206 feet per second [7,378 m/s].

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0001000.text: Okay. Got about 1,500 feet to go.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0001000.text: It's pretty damn nominal, isn't it, so far?

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0001000.text: 14, Houston. Predicted cut-off is as planned, 11 plus 43.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0001000.text: Predicted time of shutdown; 11 minutes, 43 seconds. We're now at 11 minutes, 10 seconds.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0001000.text: Apollo 14, Houston. Predicted cut-off 11 plus 43 nominal. Over.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0001000.text: Downrange distance now at 1,322 nautical miles [2,448 km]. 11 minutes, 30 seconds.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0001000.text: Shutdown. We'll stand by now for preliminary orbital readings both onboard and from the ground.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0001000.text: Apollo 14, Houston. The booster is safed and your orbit is Go.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0001000.text: Roger. Good show. Go orbit; booster safe.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0001000.text: TVC Servo Power, two, coming Off now. [Long pause.]

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0001000.text: 14, Houston. I have a Z-torquing angle when you're ready to copy.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0001000.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We're advised that the Vice President of the United States is now in the firing room. We will switch to Cape Kennedy.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0001000.text: Okay, three BMAG s going to Rate 2.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0001000.text: Apollo 14, Houston. The Saturn is configured for orbit. We're showing you in a 102 circular orbit...

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0001000.text: Okay, Gordon, I'll take the Z-torquing angle.

a14-t-0001000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0001000.text: Roger, Stu. The Z-torquing angle is a plus 0.14. Over.

a14-t-0001500.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0001500.text: 14, Houston. You have 45 seconds to Vanguard LOS . There'll be about a 40-second gap to Canary.

a14-t-0001500.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0001500.text: Apollo 14, Houston. How do you read through Canary?

a14-t-0001500.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0001500.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. Now at 22 minutes into the flight of Apollo 14. We're less than 2 minutes away now from Loss Of Signal with Canary. Apollo 14 presently in a circular orbit of 102 nautical miles [189 km]. At this time, we will play back the tapes of our conversations with 14 just following our switch back to the Cape.

a14-0002200.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0002200.text: 14, Houston. About 45 seconds to LOS . We have nothing for you before Carnarvon. Over.

a14-0002200.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0002200.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 25 minutes now since lift-off. We're out of acquisition range with Canary at this time. We expect to reacquire the spacecraft over Carnarvon in approximately 27 minutes. At 25 minutes into the flight of Apollo 14, this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0002500.text: Down here somewhere. There, you're getting close.

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0002500.text: Don't see it. There it comes.

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0002500.text: Okay. Main Reg B valve, Open; and A valve, Closed.

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0002500.text: Okay. Here, let me get you started on your optics.

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0002500.text: Can I borrow that [garble] back again? Oh, there she be.

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0002500.text: Okay. Ready for your optics, Stuart?

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0002500.text: No, not quite yet. Let me get my handholds down here, so...

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0002500.text: Okay. Well, holler when you're ready, and I'll come back to you.

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0002500.text: Well, I'm a little behind on...

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0002500.text: ...Carnarvon LOS , now. Okay, Service Module RCS monitor check. I've got all eight of them gray. Okay. 115 to 140 75. That all looks good. Helium Press...

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0002500.text: Okay. Can I help you with anything now?

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0002500.text: You can read the helium pressures - I'll - I'll get those. I just thought that...

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0002500.text: Now, why did they put those that way?

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0002500.text: ...quantity's 100 and full scale high and tank temp is 74.

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0002500.text: You got tank temp down there?

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0002500.text: ...Let me just get the pressures and then the tanks and the quantities, because I have to copy them all down.

a14-t-0002500.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0002500.text: 41 on B. Now, what do you need?

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay. That's helium - I need manifold Press.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay. Manifold pressure is 200 on D...

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0003000.text: 200 on C.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0003000.text: 200 on B.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0003000.text: And 200 on A.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Very good.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0003000.text: [Garble].

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay. Helium tank temp - I need to record.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay. Tank temp's on A at 75.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0003000.text: B is 72; C is 81; and D is 77.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay. Propellant quantity.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0003000.text: B, full scale high...

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0003000.text: C, full scale high; D is full scale high; A is full scale high. That baby had a full load.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay. Okay, Command Module RCS monitoring. Talkback, gray.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: I'll get the cameras in a little bit.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Yes. Okay, we're in no hurry...

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: I'm going to read my optics dust cover jettison.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Shepard
a14-t-0003000.text: Yes. We didn't have to worry about the cameras before.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: Yes.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: That looks good...

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay. Install optics eyepieces and handles...

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: ...that's done. G/N Power, Optics, on (up).

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: ...Manifold Press 81 to 105. That's good. Those are good. Okay. Secondary radiator leak check.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: Optics Zero, Off.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: [Garble] quantity...

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: Optics Zero, Zero.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Al, could I have the Secondary Glycol to Radiator valve...

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: Optics Mode, Man.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: ...Normal for 30 seconds and then Bypass.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: Optics Coupling [garble] Direct; Optics Speed control, Hi.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay. That'll be 15 seconds. Okay, let's see if we've got the monitor. Optics hand control, okay, is Manual, Hi, Direct, and going max right. Going about 40 degrees. And this one ought to go about 150.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: Man! It looks - It's pure black. Can't see because I'm not adapted. [Garble] lens cover. And you need to [garble].

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Did you get all of your jettison - optics dust cover jettison checklist, Stu?

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: Yes, I did.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Okay. G/N Optics, on. Optics Zero, Off.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: Yes.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-t-0003000.text: Zero for 15.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Roosa
a14-t-0003000.text: That's verified.

a14-t-0003000.speaker: Mitchell

a14-0005100.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0005100.text: ...Oh, gah!

a14-0005100.speaker: Roosa
a14-0005100.text: Son of a bitch! I missed that, and I could've been up there, too.

a14-0005100.speaker: Shepard
a14-0005100.text: Well, put that thing up.

a14-0005100.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0005100.text: Oh, hurry. It's not too late.

a14-0005100.speaker: Shepard
a14-0005100.text: Look right here. Look right through the hatch.

a14-0005100.speaker: Roosa
a14-0005100.text: I can't get the - All I can see is darkness.

a14-0005100.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0005100.text: Well...

a14-0005100.speaker: Shepard
a14-0005100.text: It's down that way; come up...

a14-0005100.speaker: Roosa
a14-0005100.text: Yes, just a second. Here, let me fix my couch.

a14-0005100.speaker: Shepard
a14-0005100.text: You really ought to get it, babe. Beautiful. It is beautiful!

a14-0005100.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0005100.text: That is really great. Sun comes up like thunder.

a14-0005100.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0005100.text: "This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 51 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 14. We have just acquired the Apollo 14 spacecraft through Carnarvon. We'll quickly pass on to you heart rates during lift-off on the Command Module Pilot and Lunar Module Pilot. Stu Roosa's..."

a14-0005100.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0005100.text: Apollo 14, Houston through Carnarvon. How do you read?

a14-0005100.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0005100.text: We read you loud and clear.

a14-0005100.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0005100.text: Roger. We're reading you a lot of background static. [Pause.]

a14-0005100.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0005100.text: Houston, are you ready for our IMU REFSMMAT realign check, P52 numbers?

a14-0005100.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0005100.text: Roger, Ed. Go ahead.

a14-0005100.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0005100.text: That's Noun 71s are 22, 24; Noun 05 is all balls; Noun 93, plus 00.085, plus 00.010, plus 00.166; GET of 38:15. And we just burst into sunlight, Gordo. It was quite a sunrise.

a14-0005100.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0005100.text: Roger, Ed. We copy that.

a14-0005100.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0005100.text: "This is Apollo Control, Houston. During this lull in communications we'll start again to pass along those heart rates at lift-off. That was a peak rate of 132 on Command Module Pilot Stu Roosa. He averaged in the 120s during the boost phase of flight. In the case of Ed Mitchell, his peak rate was 90 and ran in the 80s. Commander Alan Shepard we received no data on. We suspect a loose sensor or connector and this will be fixed sometime in orbit during the more quiet period. We presently show Apollo 14 in an orbit of 104 nautical miles [193 km] by 101 nautical miles [187 km]. We're at 54 minute

a14-0005100.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0005100.text: "This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 58 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 14, continuing here with a lull in air/ground conversation. At this time I'll pass along the shutdown times on the Saturn as it achieved its orbit: S-IC shutdown or cut-off was 2 minutes, 44 seconds; S-II shutdown was copied at 9 minutes, 19 seconds; this 3 seconds longer than nominal; and the S-IVB shutdown or cut-off was at 11 minutes, 40 seconds instead of a preflight 11 minutes, 43 seconds. We're at 59 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 14 and continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston."

a14-0005100.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0005100.text: "Apollo Control, Houston; 1 hour now into the flight of Apollo 14. We've had LOS with Carnarvon, we expect to acquire Honeysuckle momentarily. At 1 hour into the flight; this is Apollo Control, Houston."

a14-t-0006000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-t-0006000.text: Apollo 14, Houston through Honeysuckle. If you read, go omni Charlie.

a14-t-0006000.speaker: Mission Control
a14-t-0006000.text: "This is Apollo Control, Houston; 1 hour, 6 minutes now into the flight. We've had Loss Of Signal with Honeysuckle. We presently show 14 in an orbit of 106 nautical miles [196 km] by 100 nautical miles [185 km] and a velocity reading of 25,583 feet per second [7,798 m/s]. At this time we'll switch to the Cape for the postflight press conference. Switching now to the Cape."

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: But you know, you get down there, you're not adapted at all. And I'd been looking at the bright Sun; and then, I look out there. I couldn't see a thing in - in this damn thing.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Yes, you must admit we [garble] sinking feeling. Well, I was sure they were gone, because I swore I felt them go.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Okay. We're going to talk to the States, here, in a few minutes. What are we going to do, since we're ahead a little bit, what do we do...

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Let me get out - while he's - I'll get out checklist here, while you're...

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Kind of look ahead and see what's next.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Yes. Yes, we've got all the cameras up.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: (Laughter) [Garble]. Do you want to use this place up here for them?

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Yes, that'd be good for it.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Okay. As a matter of fact, those rascals aren't bad.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: You know, those are really good work on those [Garble].

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Good workmanship, yes.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Shouldn't have that on the tape either.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: What does that say down there? Rock of Gibraltar? Take a closer look at that.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: You did do the SCS attitude reference check?

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Yes, I got it written down.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Okay. Now, the next thing we got coming up is the docking probe; and then, we get a TLI PAD; and then, we start into TLI Prep, 1 plus [Garble].

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Yes. I've got our TV camera running over here.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Do you have the - an image on the monitor?

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Uh-huh. Got the corner of the world poking out there.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: You want to put the monitor up here and can we...

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: [Garble] start to feel a little hungry.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: I am, too.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: I'm glad we decided to put those sandwiches in there.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Wonder what we got.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Well, after all, it is 5:25, Cape time.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: I must admit I got a tinge of glumness there when they called that hold. I was really primed for 3:23.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Yes, I was, too. I agree.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: I can't really blame them though.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: No, they got a - You know, you get bit once, you - you can't afford to - There's a lot of water down there. Ought to be able to [garble] coming up here.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Well, are we going to have any lunch? What do you want?

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: [Garble] 20 degrees of angle.

a14-0010600.speaker: Unknown crew member
a14-0010600.text: (Whistling)

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Well, let's see, [garble] get a little time here. Let's take a look at this COAS . Put it on the horizon and see what it reads.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: (Groan)

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Pull this out of here.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Yes, just push me around if I'm in your way.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: [Garble] 14, 14. 14 and a half. Whoops!

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Would you like to see out my window, guys?

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Look at that. Good picture.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Now, if you want to hold it, let me see if I can peak it up here. It drifted away from me is the reason I - f/44, brighten it up. Okay. I think f/44 is what I want.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Pretty good.

a14-0010600.speaker: Unknown crew member
a14-0010600.text: (Cough)

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: [Garble] resolution, haven't we?

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Yes.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: At least the black-and-white does.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: I'm looking to the north, aren't I - as we're going along?

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: You better be.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: You - you - straight out that window is not too far off the track, I mean, you know...

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Straight out this window?

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Yes, you know...

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Oh...

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: You can almost see the nadir out that window. Oh, - you're, - oh, - well, I didn't realize you were down on that window.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Well, I was looking out...

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: You're - both...

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: ...of both of them.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: ...windows on your side.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Yes, out this one [garble].

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: You know, I can't believe how clean that this spacecraft is.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: I haven't seen a single bolt...

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Okay. Let me have that a minute, Stu.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: [Garble].

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: The only thing cluttering it up are the backup patches.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: [Garble].

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Hold the cabin just a second, Stu. Let me see if I can anchor this monitor any better.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Okay. Yes, it - it's set up on that Velcro. It - it should seat where you...

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Well, it seems to be. I keep kicking it off. Here, let me...

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Need a little more cord there.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: That's all I - that's all I need is a little more cord.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Yes. In lunar orbit, I'm going to be swamped with cord and cable.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: What's that?

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: There's more badges (laughter).

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Okay, I got it.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: I'll get it out of the way [garble] I'm over here. [garble] beep, beep, beep all over the place.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: He who laughs last.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Well I'm - even so, I'm hell of a lot happier that we're flying and looking at their patches, rather than the other way around.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Well, That's what I meant by laughing last (laughter ).

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Yes. It's really a strange feeling. You know, sitting here looking out, it's hard to tell whether you're standing on your head, or...

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Yes, I'm just - I'm still just a bit disoriented.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Are you?

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Well, I'm not when I look out the window, but I'm still - I'm a little bit disoriented in direction.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Well, I think the only aloof feeling you have is just the fact that you're stuffy [garble] feeling in your head.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Yes.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: [Garble] if I thought you could [garble] things looking so [garble].

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: What you got going for you there, Leader?

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Huh?

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: What you got going for you there?

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Oh, I was just - you know - looking around; see if I can get disoriented. [Garble].

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Oh. It sounds like...

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Up is up, and down is down.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: No sweat!

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Sure am anxious to get this thing burning again.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Yes. Yes. I tell you, I'd be a little bit nervous about the, the way that baby put us in orbit!

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Yes. How's our tanks going? I guess we ought to take a look at those over here.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: 35 - 35, oxidizer; and 20, fuel. Right where it was when she cut off.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Well, I guess I'd better put this back until we get to Houston, here, in a minute.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Well, we're 01:28:46, now. My checklist says US LOS - Oh, okay. LOS , sorry about that. [Garble].

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: That shouldn't change.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Yes. We ought to have them.

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Ought to be fairly close.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: There, we just - we just got a wiggle on - yes...

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Here it comes.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: [Garble]. It's not worth shit.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: No. It's not very good.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: There, it's coming up.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Okay.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Hello, Houston; Apollo 14. How do you read?

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: [Garble] coastline [garble] I - I can see it,

a14-0010600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0010600.text: Ah, there it is. Yes. See? That's Baja.

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Yes.

a14-0010600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0010600.text: Yes?

a14-0010600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0010600.text: Hello, Houston; Apollo 14. How do you read?

a14-0010600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0010600.text: "This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 1 hour and 30 minutes now since the lift-off of Apollo 14. We presently show 14 less than a minute now away from acquisition, with an orbit of 106 by 101 nautical miles [196 by 187 km]. A preliminary look at our Translunar Injection burn puts it at a time of 2 hours, 28 minutes, 27 seconds."

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Apollo 14, this is Houston. You're loud and clear, Ed. [Long pause.]

a14-0013000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0013000.text: Where is it? I can't see it.

a14-0013000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0013000.text: I - I'm not sure it is - I can't - I've got a...

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Apollo 14, Houston. You're loud and clear. Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: Roger, Houston. We've completed our checklist up to page [garble].

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: 14, Houston. We started getting - pretty bad static right in the middle of that transmission. Will you say again?

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: Roger, Houston. We have completed our [garble] L2-18.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: Houston, we're starting to extend the docking probe now.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Roger, Ed. And I have a TLI plus 90 PAD any time you're ready to copy.

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: Roger. One second and I'll be ready for you. [Long pause.]

a14-0013000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0013000.text: Okay, Houston, the probe's extended. [Pause.]

a14-0013000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0013000.text: Houston, I'm ready to copy.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Okay, Ed. One question from Dr. Gilruth. They're wondering how y'all like zero g.

a14-0013000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0013000.text: Say again, Houston.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Dr. Gilruth was wondering how you like to fly - how you like flight in zero g...

a14-0013000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0013000.text: I think I got that one, Gordon. You're asking about zero g and it's - it's really great. Everybody's in great shape, we're having a ball, well ahead of the timeline.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Roger, I'll go ahead with TLI plus 90, Ed, if you're ready.

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: Go ahead.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Okay, it's a TLI plus 90, SPS / G&N . Noun 47, 64470; minus 1.45, plus 1.30; T IG is 003:59:51.13; Noun 81, minus 0515.8, plus all balls, plus 8420.6; attitude, 181, 256, 001; H A is NA; H P , plus 0017.1; 8436.4, 9:01, 8404.9; sextant star, 15; 221.4, 39.9; boresight star is NA; Noun 61, minus 30.14, minus 025.00; 1154.4, 33721; GET for .05g, 012 - correction - 010:57:29. GDC Align set stars are Sirius and Rigel; 333, 083, 013; no ullage. Go ahead.

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: Roger, Houston. That comm wasn't too good. I missed burn time, trunnion angle, and [pause] Please repeat those two. [Long pause.]

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Roger. Your burn time is 9:01 and trunnion angle, 39.9. Over.

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: Roger. And say again the burn time.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Burn time 9:01, 9:01. Over.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Okay, Ed. I have about four corrections. The first is on Delta-V X on Noun 81. I missed your readback on that. It should be minus 0515.8. Is that what you got?

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: That's affirm; 0515.8.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Okay; a couple of read-backs were incorrect. Trunnion angle is 39.9, 39.9. Over.

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: Roger; trunnion, 39.9.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: And on R-aligns, or the GDC align, that is 333, and pitch is 083. Yaw you read back correctly, 013. Over.

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: Roger; 333, 083, and you're coming in very loud and clear now, Gordon.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Okay, Ed. You've been loud and clear. I'll give you the P37 for Lift-off plus 8, if you're ready.

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: Go ahead.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Okay, GET of ignition is 008:00, 3283, minus 165, and GET for 400K, 045:38. Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Roger, your readback's correct, and I have the TLI PAD.

a14-0013000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0013000.text: Okay, these PADs are sure wrecking my viewing, but all right. [Pause.]

a14-0013000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0013000.text: Okay, Houston, go ahead with the TLI PAD.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: 14, Houston. Before the PAD, would you give us P00 and Accept for a new state vector?

a14-0013000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0013000.text: Okay, you have it. [Pause.]

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: And I'm ready with the TLI PAD.

a14-0013000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0013000.text: Go ahead.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Roger; time base 6 predict; 2:18:51; attitude for TLI , 179, 136, 000; burn time, 5:52; 10363.0; 35549; Sep attitude, 359, 168, 319; extraction attitude, 301, 348, 041; ejection time is 3:56:00. Go ahead.

a14-0013000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0013000.text: Okay. I have 02:18:51. I missed the angles; burn time, 5 plus 52; 10363.0, 35549; 359, 168, 319; 301, 348, 041; ejection, 3:56:00. And would you give me the angles again, please? [Long pause.]

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Roger, Al. Your readback was correct. The TLI attitude is 179, 136, 000. Go ahead.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Roger. Readback correct.

a14-0013000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0013000.text: Apollo 14, Houston. The computer's yours. We're through with the uplink.

a14-0013000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0013000.text: Okay. Thank you.

a14-0014340.speaker: Shepard
a14-0014340.text: Okay, Houston. We're going to stand by for your Go for pyro arm.

a14-0014340.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0014340.text: You're Go for pyro arm now. [Pause.]

a14-0014340.speaker: Shepard
a14-0014340.text: Okay, Houston. Our Logic switches are on.

a14-0014340.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0014340.text: Roger. Now you're Go for pyro arm.

a14-0014340.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0014340.text: We have about 4 minutes to LOS Vanguard, Ed. And, due to the launch delay, the Canary pass will be pretty low elevation, marginal; at the most, about 2 minutes long.

a14-0014340.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0014340.text: We're reading the CDR 's EKG loud and clear now. We're wondering if you did anything to fix it up there.

a14-0014340.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0014340.text: "Apollo Control, Houston; 1 hour, 47 minutes now into the flight. You heard the Translunar Injection PAD being passed to the crew. We're presently looking at a time of ignition of 2 hours, 28 minutes, 29 seconds. A Delta-V on the burn of 10,367 feet per second [3,160 m/s]. Burn duration of 5 minutes, 52 seconds. Velocity at time of shutdown, 35,549 feet per second [10,835 m/s]. As you heard CapCom Fullerton pass along, apparently we are receiving medical data from the commander at this time. We're at 1 hour, 48 minutes into the flight of Apollo 14; this is Apollo Control, Houston."

a14-0014340.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0014340.text: "Apollo Control, Houston. One hour, 50 minutes now into the flight. We..."

a14-0014340.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0014340.text: Roger; we're real close to LOS . I'll go ahead and give you the words I've got about TLI . First of all, the - the monitor angles on page L2-24 should all be increased by 2.5 degrees. And, if you're monitoring the TLI burn with the cue card, the pitch angles should all be reading about 9 degrees higher than on the card. The yaw should be within a quarter degree, one-fourth degree of what the card reads. Did you copy? Over.

a14-0014340.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0014340.text: "Apollo Control, Houston. One hour, 51 minutes. Apparently we had Loss of Signal with 14 just about the time CapCom Fullerton was passing along that new data. We repeat, we show a time of ignition for TLI of 2 hours, 28 minutes, 29 seconds. A delta velocity of - or Delta-V of 10,367 feet per second [3,160 m/s]. A burn duration of 5 minutes, 52 seconds and a velocity at time of shutdown of 35,549 feet per second [10,835 m/s]. Reacquiring with Canary."

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Okay, Houston. We got nothing of your last transmission. You dropped off the air.

a14-0015000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0015000.text: Okay, Ed. I'll start over. For the TLI - coming up on your monitor - First of all on the cue card, the yaw angles as shown are okay. The pitch that you see on the ball should be 9 degrees higher all the way through the burn than as shown on the cue card; just add 9 to all your pitch angles and that should be good. On the ORDEAL angles that - is shown on pages 2-24 and 25, increase each of those by 2 and a half degrees. At 57 minutes, instead of 18, you should have 20.5 degrees; at 59 minutes, 12.5; and at 59:55, 8.5 degrees. Over. [Long pause.]

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Roger; understand that the yaw angles are okay. Pitch should be - angle should be plus 9 degrees and ORDEAL angles increased by 2.5 degrees.

a14-0015000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0015000.text: Roger. That pitch is a 9-degree increment over what is shown on the card. In other words, all the angles should be 9 degrees higher than as shown on the card - the inertial angles. Over.

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: Roger; got you, Gordon. We got that. We're with you. [Long pause.]

a14-0015000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0015000.text: On your P15, we show that you loaded the wrong seconds figure for time base 6. Will you check it? [Long pause.]

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: Thank you, Gordon. Good call. [Long pause.]

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: 1805100. There you are. Okay. Okay, now I'll discard - this plus 2.5 degrees in depth?

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: 20.5. And this is going to become 12.5.

a14-0015000.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0015000.text: For that time to take, you're going to have to reselect P15.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Roger. I - I did, Gordon. We'll run through it again.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0015000.text: "P15 is the Saturn time base 6 initiation program."

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Okay. We need to be pressing along here.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Just a second. If you want to note that during the venting of the Delta-V test - And, under the second vent, that was minus 99.5. Okay.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0015000.text: "This is Apollo Control, Houston; one hour and 55 minutes. We had Loss of Signal with Canaries. Meanwhile the countdown clocks in Mission Control show a AOS time of 11 minutes for the Command Module. This is ARIA or an Apollo Range and Instrumentation Aircraft acquisition and we're counting down now for time of ignition. Presently showing 32 minutes, 40 seconds away from time of ignition. We're at one hour, 56 minutes into the flight, continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston."

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: I need to get a hack on that 2:18:51...

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: ...Okay, it's coming up toward 51 - Should be coming toward 55:51; that would be 5 - 23 minutes. Okay. 1...

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Okay, your number - have you got it?

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: I keep being afraid, like in the simulator, to let go of my book; it's going to fall down on the...

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: Yes, [garble]. That's what you get for not paying attention to what you're doing.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: That's the next thing. Now first, EMS Function, Delta-V .

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: And, Stu, check your DAP , if you haven't already.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Okay. We're setting our ORDEAL at 100/Earth.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: I want to be sure that GDC is right on the money. Within a quarter of a degree. Okay, that's close enough. Okay. GDC 's aligned, Ed.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Okay. We want Earth power. We want 100. That's what we have. Okay.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: And it says we can arm the pyros here.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Is that time correlated at all or is the...

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Yes, it says here that we have - It's right after LOS at Carnarvon at 1:55, and we're 3 minutes - 4 minutes after that. [Garble].

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: SECS Pyro, two - SECS Pyro Arm, two, on (up).

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Okay, all I do with the ORDEAL at this time is set Earth power in 100 and hold that.

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: Why don't you slew it in - Well, see, you call a Verb 83. It says you set ORDEAL , so...

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: Yes, you really want to set the ORDEAL up on Verb 83.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Okay. Okay, so we'll select ball 1 to Orb Rate and we will hold it back; then we'll slew up to 1.0. [Garble] Okay, ORDEAL 's running at 1.5. Operating Slow, Earth/100. Okay.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Okay. And standing by for pyro arm.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Rotational Control Power, Normal, two, AC/DC, verify.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Rot Control Power Direct, two, Main A/Main B.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Direct 1, Main A/Main B; Direct 2, Main A/Main B.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Launch Vehicle Indicator, GPI - S-II / S-IVB , verify.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Okay. GPI is in S-II / S-IVB . And that's - The pressures are real quiet down here.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: We've got to remember to watch those babies after shutdown, too.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Okay. Circuit breaker Direct Ullage, two, closed.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Okay, two Ullage breakers going closed.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: And I'm cycling the cryo fans.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Okay. [Garble] see how close that baby is before we - [garble].

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: [Garble] 1 minute. 17, 18, 19, 20. Hey, it stayed right in there, didn't it? Two hours; no appreciable error. [garble] Enter. Reset.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Okay. And Stu has lunar time base 6.

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: Yes, I was looking at Noun 20 there.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Okay, Control is coming up. It's locked.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Time base 6 is at 2:18. And we have 16 minutes to stand by.

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: Stand by, in case we just have to [garble].

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: No, God damn it! That's the way we play it.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: That's what the damn thing's there for.

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: Think positive and prepare for the worst.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Okay. Tell me, how - Where do we stand now with respect to sunlight. We shouldn't get sunlight prior to...

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Well, 2:21 on the old time line.

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: It's going to be earlier because sunset was a little early. We have three - three-quarters of an hour - 15 degrees [Garble].

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Did we really get off at 03? Is that about what it was?

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: Yes. See - It looks like they programed us for 40-minutes-late lift-off and that's what we have.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: You know, I been getting light flashes with my eyes open.

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: I think you should when you see lightning down there. Ed and I saw some when you were copying that TLI PAD.

a14-0015000.speaker: Shepard
a14-0015000.text: Okay. I see a forest fire down there.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0015000.text: We were over Africa at the start...

a14-0015000.speaker: Roosa
a14-0015000.text: Say hello to all the troops at Mozambique. Hello, troops in Mozambique.

a14-0015000.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0015000.text: "This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 2 hours, 4 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 14. We presently show 14 in an orbit of 106.2 nautical miles [196.7 km] by 102.4 nautical miles [189.6 km]. Our latest update on the Translunar Injection burn shows a time of ignition of 2 hours, 28 minutes, 30 seconds; a Delta-V of 10,366.5 feet per second [3,159.7 m/s]; burn duration of 5 minutes, 52 seconds; predicted velocity at time of shutdown, 35,551.8 feet per second [10,836.2 m/s]; an altitude at time of cut-off of 173 nautical miles [320 km]. The Go No/Go callup for TLI will be made after acquisitio

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Damn, except for the - the dynamics during launch, it seemed like a Sim, you know it?

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Uh-huh.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Sitting here, quiet. The visual's a little better.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: This seems to be a light flashing by. [Garble].

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: (Humming - "Give My Regards to Broadway")

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: You shouldn't be rolling.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Huh?

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: You shouldn't be rolling.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Now, I see something to do here.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Yes, I'm going to go back - and make sure we haven't missed a single thing.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: I got the G&N Dictionary down here. All out, ready to read.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Let's just be sure we haven't missed anything on the checklist.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Did they get us shafted on the [garble] on that LOS ?

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Yes.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Let's see. We want [garble] 20 degrees [garble] and we're making...

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: No, 10 degrees.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Yes. Yes, 10. And we're making 4 degrees a minute. So, it should change our AOS time - I mean our sunrise time to 2 and a half minutes [Garble].

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: [Garble].

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: And it should be earlier. Sunset should be earlier and sunrise should be earlier. Well, what does that work out for sunrise?

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Okay. [Garble] looking at our fuel pressure - I mean, oxidizer pressure should stay at 36 - 35, and fuel at 20.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Okay, Al, do you want to check your DAC and make sure its settings are it - on it like you want it, to get it done. T8 at 250th.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Okay. Let me check it for you. I've got a T8, and it's focused at 7 feet. I've got a 250th.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Okay. Twelve frames...

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Twelve frames a second.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Magazine A.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Magazine A.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Got an 18-millimeter lens with the right-angle mirror on it.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Exactly.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Okay. I'm going to set up the Hasselblad then.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Okay. We're 9 and a half minutes from time base 6.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Okay.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Yes, I'm glad you called that, Ed. It shows you what you can do. I had apparently knocked that thing to 24 frames per second.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Really?

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Yes. It's now sitting at 12.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Okay. Let's, just for the hell of it, take some pictures of that - top of that booster anyway, huh?

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Yes, I'm going to try to. You mean with the Hasselblad or what?

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Yes, the Hasselblad.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Yes, with the Hasselblad. We're supposed to do it only, you know, provided it locks anomalous to us, but I think we ought to just go ahead and take a few pictures...

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Yes, I think we ought to...

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Oh, yes. I think we ought to take a couple as we come off. And then, when we roll and it comes in the hatch window, I think you ought to take a couple out of the hatch window.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Have you got a range sight on the camera?

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: No, not right now. Wouldn't hurt if we did, but we don't.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Yes, I got myself all strapped in now.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Okay. ASA 64.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Okay. Time base 6 for a start, and then, we'll have sunrise. And then, we'll do all those good things,

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Then we'll get AOS from Carnarvon. We'll get a Go for TLI , and we'll burn the son of a gun.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Beautiful.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Some ride.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: [Garble] I have to get closer. [Garble].

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Some ride.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: There was no doubt in your mind of lift-off, I was a little surprised at the level of the vibration prior to lift-off though. I'd been led to believe it was probably worse. Maybe they're strapping us in tighter nowadays.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: I didn't have any trouble with communications or anything.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Oh, it was beautiful all the way. Boy, that BPC goes, doesn't it? That tower, son of a bitch moves out. I didn't even notice the switches being hard (laughter). I didn't figure I would.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: (Yawn)

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: I didn't figure I would. Man, it was beautiful! All the checks right on the mark. Played her right like the sim. [Garble] just like the simulator.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: I guess, in order to make sure we don't screw that up, I guess I'd better pull that dark slide out right now. Right there.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: [Garble] yet.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Yes, but I don't want to - be ready to take a picture and miss a picture because of it.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Anybody want any water?

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Yes. I'll take a slug of water.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: [Garble] a good place to leave that baby [garble].

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: How long before time base 6?

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Oh, about 5 minutes.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: I'm getting kind of hungry. I'm going to have to watch my weight. I'm going to really slurp it up at the table tonight...

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: [Garble] up in there.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Well, [garble] be back [garble].

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Pretty tasty water.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Well, there goes the monitor. Watch out for the trim.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: I tell you, this weightlessness is really great, isn't it?

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Yes, I'll enjoy it.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Zero g. Fantastic!

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: I want to see the stars out there.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: I don't feel any - any more stuffy than I did this morning.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: I'm - I'm kind of surprised at that, too. I - I think Al Bean made the comment that everybody's face looked puffed up.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Yes?

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Your face doesn't look puffed up to me, particularly,

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: I'm sure there is some adjustment...

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Yes.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: ...you adjust to the - You know, the old - your cardiovascular - relaxes. [Garble].

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: I just feel great, personally.

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Well, hell, after the goddamn launch like that, who couldn't feel great?

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: Oh, I've got a little stuffiness in my head, I...

a14-0020400.speaker: Shepard
a14-0020400.text: Yes,

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: You know, it sort of feels like you're - maybe when you're pulling 1 and a half or 2g's with a - with a cold.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0020400.text: Yes.

a14-0020400.speaker: Roosa
a14-0020400.text: It sort of feels just like it.

a14-0020400.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0020400.text: "This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 2 hours, 16 minutes now into the flight of Apollo 14. We'll stand by for any communications with the ARIA aircraft. We're 12 minutes, 25 seconds away from time of ignition."

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: I can't help but feel I'm laying on my back.

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: I sort of feel like I'm laying head down somewhere. Maybe that's because of the...

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Like resting on the sit-up board at...

a14-0021600.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0021600.text: Apollo, Houston; this - Apollo 14, this is Houston through ARIA 4. How do you read?

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: Houston, this is Apollo 14. Loud and clear. How me?

a14-0021600.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0021600.text: Roger. You're readable; a little bit in the background noise, but loud and readable.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0021600.text: "That was Ed Mitchell responding aboard the spacecraft."

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: When did we say it was going to be?

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: Okay, Houston; 14. How do you read now?

a14-0021600.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0021600.text: Apollo 14, Houston. You're readable, too. Go ahead.

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: Okay, I was just checking the comm here. Gee, you're just beautiful; the ARIA is really putting out for us.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0021600.text: "We're ten minutes away now, from time of ignition."

a14-0021600.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0021600.text: Roger. I guess this is the best ever for ARIA .

a14-0021600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0021600.text: "2 minutes 18 seconds, that was Stu Roosa coming in with a comment."

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Eighty seconds to time base 6 start, troops.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: Launch Vehicle Guidance to IU, verify.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Launch Vehicle Guidance to IU. Never has moved.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Although we were ready for it...

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: Standing by for the Uplink Activity light.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: I want you to mark when that Sun comes over the horizon.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: All right. You want to not look at it?

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Well, it's right in my window.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Thirty seconds to start of time base 6,

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: We get an Uplink Activity light and an S-II Sep light.

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: Okay. We have an S-II Sep light.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Yes, it looked like it was a little late, didn't it? When that light goes out, I'm going to start my timer.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: Okay. Count down to the Sun.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Okay. The light's out. Timer starting.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: And counting. Watch the sunrise in your eye, Al.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Okay. Tank pressure's 35 and 20. That looks good.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Okay. Is the Sun on time?

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: it's just - just a little early.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: Okay. Master Alarm, O 2 Flow Hi.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: You have a - Direct O 2 valve?

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: It's holding inside the cabin. Forgot to trigger it. I'll have - Well, hell, it's down below the Go mark. It can't be.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: It's just a transient. Had to be.

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: Turn your suit regulator over there. Just turn it - it's on Both. Turn it up to 1...

a14-0021600.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0021600.text: Roger; we missed if you did call time base 6 starting. We'd like to know how the tank pressures look; over.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Okay, it looked to us like time base started within 1 second of nominal time, and the oxidizer tank is currently - quietly - at 37 and the [garble] tank is currently setting quietly at 26.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: You're going to get Up TLM...

a14-0021600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0021600.text: "That was Alan Shepard responding to that call. We're at 2 hours, 22 minutes now. 6 minutes, 25 seconds away from time of ignition."

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: ...We command Block on both of them.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: FDAI - ORDEAL FDAI 1, Orb Rate; 2, Inertial.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Okay; 1 is Orb Rate, 2 is Inertial.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: And we're standing by to slew to 20.5 at - at 57.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: We're a little bit ahead of that, in fact. 54, 55...

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Eight degrees - would be 28 and a half at 55.

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: Yes, you know we did that in the sim - got fouled up on that, too.

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: Is the tape recorder barber pole? Okay. I guess they're not getting data up right now. We're still through the ARIA . I guess we haven't got...

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: No, we've lost the LOS on the ARIA .

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: And I'll bet what happens is, if the suit accumulator cycles, it might kick that over to the...

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Okay. I think I've got my Orb Rate ball set up where we can check it again in another minute. Tank pressures are reading 40. We're out of comm with them now, are we?

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: We should have them again here in about 2 minutes.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Tank pressures look good. Oxidizer, 39, fuel's coming up to 40. Beautiful, S-IVB . At 56 minutes, we should be at 24 and a half.

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: I thought that Sun was shining...

a14-0021600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0021600.text: "Four minutes away now from time of ignition."

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: My Orb Rate ball is exactly right.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0021600.text: "We now are receiving Carnarvon data, and very shortly Flight Director Pete Frank will poll this flight control team as to our status for TLI ."

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Did you notice that that VHF volume being full up distorted the...

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: I couldn't understand why he sounded so garbled there.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Okay. Coming up on 57. It should be 20.5.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: It's now 21 [garble] right about there. Yes, look at that mother.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Okay. We are 57 minutes now and we're 20.5.

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: Okay, Houston; 14. How do you read us?

a14-0021600.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0021600.text: Roger, 14; this is Houston through Carnarvon, and you're loud and clear.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0021600.text: "2 minutes, 20 - 2 hours, 26 minutes. Pete Frank now taking a status check with his flight control team. Coming up all greens."

a14-0021600.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0021600.text: You're Go for the Moon. Go for TLI .

a14-0021600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0021600.text: "That was Al Shepard responding to that Go for TLI . We're at 2 hours, 27 minutes now into the flight. One minute, 32 seconds from time of ignition."

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: It's on, right on the money.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Okay. Should be starting ullage now.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: I don't feel it or we'd be floating down.

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: Don't see any counts, do you?

a14-0021600.speaker: Roosa
a14-0021600.text: Wasn't that a 2 a minute ago?

a14-0021600.speaker: Shepard
a14-0021600.text: It probably isn't going to be as a 1. Now it's a zero.

a14-0021600.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0021600.text: Okay. At 59 minutes, Al, you should have 12 50 - 12.5. Is it after 59?

a14-0021600.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0021600.text: "Less than 30 seconds away now from time of ignition. Our displays show a predicted apogee resulting from this burn of a 250,263.7 nautical miles [463,488.4 km]. We're at 2 hours, 28 minutes now into the flight. Standing by."

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: S-II Sep light out on time.

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Okay. Right on the money, 8.5. Operate/Slow.

a14-0022800.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0022800.text: Roger, and we show good thrust on the S-IVB .

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "That's Al Shepard, spacecraft commander giving that report."

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: It knows what it's doing. 28, 29, 30. Okay, at 30, it should come on 129 - and it's very close.

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Yes, Michael Wash [?] gave us the right numbers. We're right on cue.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: At 1 minute, it should be at 120 - 128.

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Slight vibration, coming along very smooth.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "Booster says we look good; 1 minute, 3 seconds into the burn."

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Okay. 128, on the money. A little low in altitude.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "Flight dynamics is pleased with the agreement between his data."

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: All those g's make me hungry.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "We show a velocity buildup on one of our displays presently reading 27,390 feet per second [8,348 m/s]."

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Yes, but it got my stomach to realizing I was hungry.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Okay, tank pressures are still good.

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Houston. Tank pressures are steady at 40 and 30.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "Al Shepard again from aboard the spacecraft."

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Must have been a PU-use shift.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Man, that's like cutting in the AB.

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Yes. Seven-tenths of a g now.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: Yes, it sure is. Got the monitor right in my lap.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: A little low on my card.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: But the angles are good. Maybe the buildup data isn't too striking, you know.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "Still receiving data showing the velocity of 29,212 feet per second [8,904 m/s]."

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Keep analyzing. Here comes Key Release. Key Release. Key Release, Stu.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: No, that's - that's just to go back to now.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Okay. Yes, I've got a 62 over an 80.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "3 minutes, 10 seconds now into the burn."

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: It does change vibration modes with the mass, doesn't it?

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: 117 - We're 114, 1050, 30. It's a little - running a little low.

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: We only pitching about 1 degree right now.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: Feels kind of heavy, doesn't it?

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "Network reports we're receiving IU data through Guam. Looks good."

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "Apollo 14 tracking right down the middle of our plot boards in Mission Control."

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Okay. It's back to about zero on the ball.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Okay. Five minutes. H-dot's a tad low, altitude's a little low, and the velocity's just about in the money. Okay. We're looking for 35...

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Okay, let us talk about what we're going to do.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: We're going to see that on the DSKY . And then we're going to shut down.

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: We're getting a yaw in here, too.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "That was Alan Shepard reporting shutdown. It looks like..."

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: [Garble] are venting down. The oxidizer is coming down through 35 now. The fuel is coming down through 30.

a14-0022800.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0022800.text: Apollo 14. Roger on the vent. [Long pause.]

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: No, no, no. Bit Rate, Low.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: Yes, yes, I got it. EMS Mode, Standby.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "Apollo Control, Houston. That shutdown time appeared to be right on time."

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Reading a V I , plus 35542; Delta-V C , minus 8.8, H-dot plus 04399, H-pad, plus 01747 [Long pause.]

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: Okay. Let's start again. EMS Mode, Standby; EMS Function, Off.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: EMS Mode, Standby; EMS Function, Off.

a14-0022800.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0022800.text: 14, this is Houston. We copy V I , plus 35542, Delta-V C of minus 8.8, and missed the last two? Would you repeat?

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Okay. I'm not sure I got your H-dot readback. It's plus 04399.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mission Control
a14-0022800.text: "With that report, Flight Dynamics Officer Dave Reed says that it looks like a good burn. We're at 2 hours, 37 minutes now into the flight. We'll stand by and continue to monitor."

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: Okay, FDAI number 1, Inertial; RHC number 2, locked.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Okay, FDAI number 1 is now Inertial; RHC number 2 is now locked.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: And Stu is going to Pro and to P00 .

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Okay. Let me get the Activity light out.

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: How close did that baby cut out?

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: Within 7 feet per second, it looks like.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: Okay, and let's see. Your H-dot's 4399 - You said that's good.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: H - the H was low. See, we were low all the way. That may have been the design or something.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: Okay, CMC Activity light out, key Verb - key Verb 66 Enter, Stu.

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: I'll have to get that. We got [garble].

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: Did you get your FDAI 1 - number 1 to Inertial off?

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Houston. On the S-IVB, oxidizer pressure is now down around 18 and fuel pressure is about 17.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: And, Stu, did you get - put the Waste Stowage Vent valve to Close?

a14-0022800.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0022800.text: Roger. I understand; 18 and 17 on the tank pressures.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: We still have comm with him?

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Okay, I guess he's reading us.

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: What are you going to do about your connections?

a14-0022800.speaker: Shepard
a14-0022800.text: Oh, look at us climb away.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Let's see. Let me get this Waste Stowage Vent before...

a14-0022800.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0022800.text: Yes;, Waste Stowage Vent valve, Closed.

a14-0022800.speaker: Roosa
a14-0022800.text: Let me see, I'm turning off...

a14-0023857.speaker: Fullerton
a14-0023857.text: You're loud and clear, Ed. And we should have continuous voice and data from here on out. You're loud and clear through Guam.

a14-0023857.speaker: Mitchell
