And what they'd like them to do is have the camera pointing through the docking window of the LM , the upper window, right at the vent and run it 20 seconds' worth at 24 frames [per second]. [Long pause.]

a14-0594954.speaker: Roosa
a14-0594954.text: Okay. They'll boresight on the vent and run her 20 seconds at 24 frames.

a14-0594954.speaker: Haise
a14-0594954.text: Okay, then they'd like to change the frame rate to one [frame per second] and run the camera for another 20 seconds. [Long pause.]

a14-0594954.speaker: Roosa
a14-0594954.text: Okay. Change to one frame per second and run 20 seconds.

a14-0594954.speaker: Haise
a14-0594954.text: Okay. After that chore, they can rest a while and wait until you get down to the end of the water dump, Stu, and you can kind of give them the word when you're ready to shut her off. And then they'd like them to shoot the vent again at 24 frames a second for 10 seconds. [Long pause.]

a14-0594954.speaker: Roosa
a14-0594954.text: [Garble] the vent [garble].

a14-0594954.speaker: Haise
a14-0594954.text: Stand by 1, Stu, we got pretty bad comm now.

a14-0594954.speaker: Haise
a14-0594954.text: And, Stu, how do you read me now?

a14-0594954.speaker: Roosa
a14-0594954.text: Loud and clear, Fred.

a14-0594954.speaker: Haise
a14-0594954.text: Okay. We left off with them shooting 24 frames [per second] for 10 seconds when you turn the valve off.

a14-0594954.speaker: Roosa
a14-0594954.text: That's affirmative.

a14-0594954.speaker: Haise
a14-0594954.text: Okay. Then they're to change the frame rate to one frame per second and run the camera for at least 60 seconds or until cloud particles are no longer visible. But I guess if neither of those two events happen in that time, they're not to run it longer than about 180 seconds' worth. [Pause.]

a14-0594954.speaker: Haise
a14-0594954.text: In other words, they're trying - they'd like to get a picture of the last drop there, Stu. [Long pause.]

a14-0594954.speaker: Roosa
a14-0594954.text: Okay. They'll change to one frame per second for at least 60 seconds or until no vent, and max time will be 180 seconds.

a14-0594954.speaker: Haise
a14-0594954.text: Yeah, that's it. Then the only thing else is, you can frisk them when they get back and make sure they got your 18-millimeter lens and the Mag F back across, and they should put the 10 millimeter back on the LM camera.

a14-0594954.speaker: Roosa
a14-0594954.text: Roger. I'm having Al sign a receipt for the Command Module property in here before it leaves.

a14-0594954.speaker: Haise
a14-0594954.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a14-0594954.speaker: Haise
a14-0594954.text: And, 14, we're going to have a site changeover here directly. We may lose you for a minute or so.

a14-0594954.speaker: Roosa
a14-0594954.text: Okay.

a14-0601201.speaker: Haise
a14-0601201.text: Okay. I guess we've successfully did the switchover.

a14-0601527.speaker: Roosa
a14-0601527.text: Okay, Fred. I'd like to question you here, since we've had this change in the Flight Plan, about going to the Wide Deadband here. If I do that, then it'll be another maneuver back to start the PTC , where if I stay Narrow Deadband, I could be damping the rates when I got ready to start the PTC . Would you smoke that over there and see what you think about that?

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Houston, 14.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Stand by, 14, until we get a little better comm.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: 14, Houston.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, I thought I heard you call a while ago.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Houston, do you read 14?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. I'm reading you about 3 by 3. Go ahead with your message. [Pause.]

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Hello, Houston. Do you read 14? [Pause.]

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Houston, do you read 14?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: 14, Houston.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay, Freddo. We're reading you loud and clear.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. We got good signal strength again here.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. You're coming in now.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Okay, Fred. I didn't hear back from you and I wanted to get to the roll on this time around because it'll be too late the next one. So I'm going to go ahead and go in the narrow deadband. It looks to me like it would be - we'd save gas that way. [Pause.]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. He was still trying to crank out some numbers to compare there, Stu. [Pause.]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Freddo. You've faded out again. We've lost you. [Long pause.]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: How do you read now? [Long pause.]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: 14, Houston. How do you read? [Long pause.]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: 14, Houston. We'd like Omni Alpha. [Long pause.]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: And - Houston, 14. How do you read now?

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Houston, this is 14. You're loud and clear.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. The narrow deadband looks like it'll save you a little gas there, Stu.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Okay. I didn't hear back from you so I wanted to catch the roll this time around. So I went ahead and went Narrow.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Houston. I'm on the High Gain right now. How do you read?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Loud and clear, Ed.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: How's your PCM ? [Pause.]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. They say it looks good.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Houston, 14.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Go ahead, Ed.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: At this High Gain Antenna setting - I can - it will not switch over to Narrow Deadband [means beamwidth]; apparently. I have as much signal strength at Medium as I do in Narrow.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. We'll think about that. [Long pause.]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, 14; Houston. They'd like for you to stay in Narrow.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Roger. That's where I am.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Houston, 14.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Go ahead.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Roger. We're in the process of pressurizing the LM now, as you can probably see. We're holding for the integrity check at this point. I have the television set up and I can turn it on at your command.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, Ed. Stand by on the TV, we'll see if they're ready.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. They're all set up, Ed; you can turn it on any time.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Houston, I'm transmitting. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. We got the picture, Ed.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Roger, Houston. You should be able to recognize it. There's the Commander's number 1 window. There's its field of view at the moment. And Alan is up in the tunnel working the pressurization procedure. Stuart is coming up from under the Commander's seat - you can see his head starting to come into the field of view now - from stowing items down under the seat. Let's see if I can get a little better picture here for you. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Yes. Stu's head looks pretty good in color there. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: You mean that color wheel can handle red, Freddo?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Yes. It seems to be doing a pretty good job there. I noticed some speckles on the window there. Is that - did y'all end up with a little debris on there?

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: We have a few ice crystals, apparently, that have adhered to it from the various dumps we've made.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: You know, Freddo, that window was clean as all get out until we started all the dumping. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Houston. We're continuing the pressurization procedure. We've just opened up the pressurization valve between the two spacecraft. And we're flowing into the LM from the Command Module. Give you a picture if you can see it here. There's our cabin pressure gage, shows your quantity as well. Let's see if I can get it in view. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: A little dark and out of focus there right now, Ed.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Yes. It's a little too close. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Yes. That's a little better, I can now see the - your little card there showing the antenna patterns. But the needles on the gage is a little hard to read. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: We'll give up on that, Freddo. Our pressure is equal between the Command Module and the LM , and we will start removing tunnel hardware at this point.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: And, Houston, we're starting to shoot up into the tunnel here where - Alan Shepard is starting to pull the hatch out - if I can get him to look down for a minute and say hello to the world.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, Ed. I can see a form there that I guess is Al. It's - this picture is just a little bit dark. You can see the lights up in the tunnel.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Roger. I think we'll have just a little bit more light once this hatch gets out of the way. We have all of our floodlights on full right now. While they're doing that, let's slide out to the CDR 's window and take a look at the Moon, which happens to be right out the window. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Going to coach me a little bit, Fred, as I approach this?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, we can see it now; it's right down in the lower right quadrant of the window. The picture, though, we're seeing is a crescent, and it's really not showing too much of the detail, Ed. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. Assume you're zooming the camera now, Ed. And we lost the picture of the Moon.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. Let me try it again. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. I think what happened when you zoomed, Ed, you ended up pointing above it. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Do you see anything now, Freddo?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, it just disappeared out the lower right corner. We had it there for a little while.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. How now?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. There, it barely came in the bottom portion of the picture now. Whereabouts is the terminator now? Is that about Tranquility, somewhere in there ?

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: It's past Tranquility, and I think it's - it's approaching zero longitude at this point, I believe.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: A few hours ago we just passed Delta 'Tegnius [?], Fred.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Yes. Right, Stu.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Roger. It - I was looking through the sextant there just a minute ago. It - all of Descartes - around Descartes and the Highlands showed up real well and the terminator had just moved on over just past Platte [?]. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. And for your information, in the audience in the back here, we have most of the family in tonight - this morning down here, I should say.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Yes. 3:15 is a good time of night to have a TV show.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Prime time. Yes, that's about right in the center of the picture now. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. I've got full zoom on it, Freddo. And maybe it's too bright. Let's see if I can darken it. It'll improve the picture a little.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Yes, you're right. It's so bright, Ed, we're - we have the crescent, but not too much detail on.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Yes, that's a little better.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: And from our point of view, the Moon appears about the size of a grapefruit, held at the arm's length. It's going to get considerably bigger, and if I don't have the Earth to compare it with at the moment. But I suspect they are about the same size or maybe the Moon is starting to exceed the Earth in apparent size, [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. And the big board now has you at ...

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. We'll go ...

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Roger. Okay, I'm going to come back inside. We have now stowed the hatch. And Stu and Al are up starting to bring the probe out. And very soon we'll be able to make the trip into the LM with the camera and see what we can find in there. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: We have not, as you can obviously see, rehearsed this. Our procedures are new to us, going into the LM for the first time. And, as a matter of fact, we were a little bit rushed getting the pressurization procedure complete in order to get in on time. We'll be ready here in about 2 minutes to move on into the LM , I think. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, Ed.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: And, now, let's go back inside the Command Module. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. Are we looking up in the tunnel area now, Ed? It's pretty dark right now.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Yes, I'll be bringing the probe out ...

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Yes, I'm trying to, Fred, but it's dark. Just 1 second, I'll see if I can improve the light situation for us.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Roger. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. You're looking directly up into the tunnel now. The probe has been released from the drogue, and Stu will be bringing it straight down through the tunnel.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Yes. We got that picture in pretty good now. We can see it coming on down. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay, Houston. Al and Stu are taking the probe down under the right-hand couch now.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Roger, Ed. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Yes, we can see Al in the picture now.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. He's probably clearer for you than he is on our monitor. It's a little dark in here.

a14-0602608.speaker: Shepard
a14-0602608.text: You can look up the tunnel and see the drogue [Garbled], Ed, and I'll go and pick it up for you. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. You're looking directly at the drogue now, which is gray in color and which has a hole in the center above the capture latches. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: In our color pictures here, the opening in the drogue looks red in color. Like a big red eye.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. And Alan has it out and he's starting to come down the tunnel with it. That's probably a little dark for you, but he's coming down anyhow.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, and we've temporarily, I hope, lost our picture down here, Ed.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Fred, do you have your picture back yet?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Negative, Ed. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: And 14, the problem with the loss of picture is on our end of the street.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. Tell me when you have it back and we're ready to go through into the LM .

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: And, Ed, Houston. You may continue the commentary, I guess. It's being received out at the site and being recorded; we're just not getting it - plumbed into here.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. While we were just holding up here, Alan has slipped on through into the LM and is opening up the window shades and turning on the lights, so that as we go in, we will have some lights to give you a little better picture. I'm waiting here until - to get your picture back before I start in; however, if you would like, I'll go ahead and go into the LM .

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Stand by 1, Ed. Okay, Ed. They don't have an estimate right now. We might wait a couple of minutes; and then, I guess, if we haven't got it back, you can proceed. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. Okay, Alan's coming back through the tunnel now and it will be clear here in a minute. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Houston, while we're waiting for your picture to come back and, since it is being recorded at the site, we will take a quick station break and let Alan give us a commercial for Apollo 14.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Shepard
a14-0602608.text: Okay. Apollo 14 is progressing very nicely. As you can see, we're now right on schedule. And it looks as though the first midcourse correction is going to put us in for the lunar orbit insertion burn - very close. We're - we're currently preparing to go into the LM as Ed has told you; and, so far, everything is working very well in the Command Module. We're very pleased with the way the systems are working. Everything is quiet, going along extremely smoothly, and we have a happy little ship here. Everyone is well. Everyone is resting well. We're adapting to weightlessness, I think, very rapidl

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Roger, Al. And we have a picture back now. It's just a little bit on the dark side, but we can see you quite well.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay, Freddo. We'll start on in.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. How's that?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Hey, that's a good picture, Ed.

a14-0602608.speaker: Shepard
a14-0602608.text: Okay. We're starting through the tunnel.

a14-0602608.speaker: Shepard
a14-0602608.text: Why don't you show the docking latches while you go by, Ed. See how they look on the television. Can you see the docking latches, Freddo?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Roger. We can see those, Ed. We can see on down to the tunnel and the top of the ascent engine cover.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. I think it's significant that, in spite of our problem the other day, that when Stu - Stu finally got us into the docking ring that all of them snapped shut, which is - was very well lined up. And our docking index, as you know, cost us a case of beer, I think, because it's within 1 degree. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. And you might let us know, Ed, how you find the fit through the tunnel there.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. I'm sliding through.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Hey, was that question from Joe?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: I'm not sure he'd own up to it.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Okay. I'm through the tunnel, and I'm right at the top of the LM . I'm shining the - showing the camera down on the main console on the Commander's side. How's that picture, Freddo?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. That looks very good, Ed.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: And let's see. I'll turn it around. I'll go ahead and go on down and twist around, and maybe we can look out the window. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: And, we're now inside the LM . [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Thank you, Ed.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Can you see that, Fred?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Yes, we see what looks to be a patch there, Ed.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Is it good enough for you to read it?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Is it something like beep, beep or -

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: How did you ever guess?

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Must be some prompting from the ground.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay. And, Ed, a good portion of your swing here, the picture is a little bit on the dark side. You might try opening it up just a little bit more.

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Roger. I've had it open all the way, Freddo.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Well, I guess you can't do any better than that. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Did you find the LM pretty clean, Ed, when y'all first came aboard or was anything loose in there?

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: No, both spacecraft, Freddo, have been immaculate. I think we have found one washer floating along about 1 day ago, and we have seen nothing that was foreign to the spacecraft either before or since that time. And, as I say that, I see one floating by me right now. It may be the same washer. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Shepard
a14-0602608.text: Yes, I'd like to point out that Ed is talking about something external to the spacecraft. The cabin above the Command Module and the LM are extremely clean. We've been very pleased with the way they've looked.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Very good.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Yes, I think from what we've heard along the line, we actually expected maybe to see a few more nuts and bolts. I think a lot of credit goes to checkout crew and everything because this spacecraft is really in good shape. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: And, Freddo, I'm passing the camera back to Alan in the Command Module. We don't have enough light in here to really give you a good picture. And there's not much help from the outside since the Sun is behind us right now.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Roger, Ed. I - we got a pretty good picture of you down in the tunnel right now. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Hey, Fred. Did you hear that last comment I made about the crew and how clean the spacecraft was?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Roger, Stu.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Well, that was planted, you know, for all the authorized people that worked on the spacecraft. You know, we're really unindated [sic] with unauthorized objects in both spacecraft. I think Ed was showing you one up there, but if you could see this. I don't know if any of the backup crew is down in there tonight or not. But - okay, how about - about here - [Garbled] But, they've left their calling card. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, we have a pretty good picture of that, Stu. And, they are here.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Okay. Tell them we sure appreciate every compartment that we open up having one of these come floating out of it.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: They aim to please. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: Stu, you want to take the camera? Perhaps you can move it on up to the window. I don't know how much light there is, but sure is a good shot of the Moon out there. You might try again with the monitor so you can see what it looks like to them.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Well, we'll give it a go. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, we can see the Moon again in the number - number 1 window. It's down in the lower left corner now, Stu. Hey, that's about right in the center. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, that's - the picture's a little distorted now, Stu. It's a little bright. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Okay, that ought to help it a little.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Yes, that's about right. It's still hard to see in this picture - much in the way of detail of the features - any features on the surface. Right at the terminator, we can pick up a few craters; but, other than that, it's really hard to see very much. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Okay. Yes, I didn't think it was going to show up too much there, Fred, because that's really the way it looks with the eye. It's just now starting, you know, to get into the area where the larger craters would show up. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, we've got a good picture of Al there, now.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Okay, he's got the transfer items that he's taking up into the LM for the activation, and he might just give you a word on what they are.

a14-0602608.speaker: Shepard
a14-0602608.text: The purpose of the excursion into the LM at this time is to check out some of the communications, do a little housekeeping, look - generally look the vehicle over, and also, in this particular case, we are going to take some pictures of the Command Module while we're there. This is done during the flight on the way to the Moon to save time, so that when we actually go into the LM for the final time prior to the descent, there will be less things to do. So, I have a package of things here in my hand which I'll now be taking up into the LM and will proceed on with our housekeeping tasks up there

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, we can see him heading out with the package in hand there. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Okay, is there enough light up in there, Fred? You getting the picture?

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Roger, Stu.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: Okay.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Looks like running an obstacle course in the early going, getting by all the hoses.

a14-0602608.speaker: Roosa
a14-0602608.text: You got it. [Long pause]

a14-0602608.speaker: Mitchell
a14-0602608.text: And, Freddo, I'm starting back through the tunnel now to pick up the rest of the equipment. We have several 16- and 70-millimeter camera Mags that are being transferred over. We'll pick those up and be right back with you.

a14-0602608.speaker: Haise
a14-0602608.text: Okay, Ed.

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay, Antares; Houston. We'd like you to back out of that (P)52. We need to look at a bit here.

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Roger. Do you have some pads ready for me this pass, Fred?

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay. They're coming up in a minute, Ed. You ready to copy a couple of steps here?

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Yes. Go ahead.

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay. We'd like a VERB 11 NOUN 10 ENTER, 30 ENTER. (Pause)

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: You got it. (Long Pause)

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Do you read the DSKY, Houston? (Pause)

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Antares, Houston. What we're looking at there is the abort bit, and it looks set. And we'd like to proceed with the following to reset it.

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay. Give me the words.

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay. We need the STOP pushbutton, push. And the next thing is the ABORT pushbutton, depress. And wait on that one.

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay. Standing by on that one.

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay. I meant you can go ahead and press the ABORT button, Ed; but stand by for our word on the reset. (Pause)

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay. It's set.

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay. Stand by. (Long Pause)

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Antares, Houston. You can reset the ABORT pushbutton. (Pause)

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay. It's reset. (Pause)

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay. You can reset the STOP button...

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: (Garbled under Haise) ...Fredo?

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: You can reset the STOP button now, Ed, and press on with the P52.

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay.

a14a_1042957_to_1043237.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1042957_to_1043237.text: Okay. STOP button is reset. [About an hour later, Fred has another conversation with the Ed about the abort bit.] MP3 Audio Clip 3 mins 17 secs

a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [The next to last line at 2+09 in EdÕs checklist is "REL(ease) T(humper)/G(eophone) & Deploy - 12 slack". Two wires, each about 310-feet (94 m) long connect the experiment to the Central Station. One of the wires is connected to the thumper and carries firing signals from the thumper to the Central Station. The other wire connects three geophones placed at 10, 160 and 310 feet from the Central Station and carries seismic data collected during a period of 20 seconds before and 5 seconds after each thumper firing when the astronauts stood still. ALSEP documentation photos AS1

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: (As Ed throws something in a generally southern direction) Hey! Got pretty good range out of that baby.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Man, that thing really went, didn't it? (Pause)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Pretty good range out of that baby. (Long Pause) [Ed goes to the MET with the thumper geophone.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Al, this is Houston. Could you tell us where you are in the SIDE or PSE sequence?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Yes, sir. The legs of the SIDE have been deployed; PSE (Passive Seismic Experiment) stool is being placed 10 feet north from the Central Station.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger. [Comm Break. Ed goes back to ALSEP package 1 to release the mortar pack. He has reached 2+15 in his checklist. Al is at 2+08 in his checklist.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay, Houston. The thumper is stowed on the MET. I had to get the first geophone out in order to get it there, but we'll take care of that in a few minutes. [The geophones are attached to one of the cables. Both cables are held on reels, one at the base (geophones) one at the top (firing signals) of the thumper. Because the MET is farther out than planned, as Ed unwound the cables from the reels, the first geophone came off its reel. Later, Ed will step firmly - and carefully - on the geophone to get it properly planted in the surface. A frame from the 16-mm camera mounted on the MET shows Ed

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger, Ed. [As Ed gets back to the ALSEP package, Al may be releasing the Passive Seismic Experiment (PSE).]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Now comes the task that tries men's patience. (Pause) Getting the mortar pack off; and it's coming off, now. Incidentally, how much are you able to see, Bruce?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay, Ed. You're about one-seventh...

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: (Garbled under McCandless).

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: ...the height of our picture.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Yeah; okay. Hmm.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Went in, huh?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Yup.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay. (Pause) (Garbled) (Long Pause)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay; that's gotta be... [Comm Break. The mortar pack - M/P in the checklist - contains a set of grenades which were planned to be fired to distances of 500, 1000, 3000, and 5000 feet to the north - after the crew left the Moon, of course - in order to give larger seismic signals to give information to depths of up to 500 meters. Ed moves away from the Central Station, going 10 feet northwest, and deploys the mortar pack as per checklist.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay, Bruce. The mortar pack is in place.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [In the 1971 Technical Debrief, Mitchell indicates that, although he had a great deal of difficulty with the mortar pack during training, thanks to a lot of work and complaints to the experiment designers, when it came to the actual deployment, "we had worked with that enough in sims so that it came off about as expected."]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: And we've had interim deployment of the PSE.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger, Al. (Long Pause) [Al has put the stool and the seismometer in place, but will wait until 116:58 before he deploys the reflective skirt which will provide thermal protection.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: You know, I don't think the solar wind is going to blow our (S-band) antenna over like it generally does (in training at the Cape).

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: (Referring to his own deployment of the PSE) How about that. Steady as a rock.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay, the CPLEE (Charged Particle Lunar Environment Experiment)'s starting to come off, now. RealVideo Clip (3 min 41 sec)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Watch it, watch it, watch it, watch it, watch it, watch it.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Yup, thank you, thank you, thank you, thank you, thank you. [In the TV, we see a glint of sunlight off a cable that Al catches with his foot as he goes around the east side of the Central Station. It is almost impossible to see one's feet and it is a minor miracle that only one piece of equipment was lost to a cable pull during all of Apollo. After Ed releases the CPLEE, Al will level and align the Central Station base and then will release 16 Boyd bolts that are holding down the top of the Central Station and the thermal side-curtains. In the following, they may be re-aligning a piece of equi

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Let's see if I can get it back in line. Can you tap it toward me a little? We're a little too close, if we can get this whole thing a little further away. Kind of push it with your foot.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Evans
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Kitty Hawk, Houston. In the blind here. Looks like about - coming upon T 1 time for Dollond E.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: I don't want to get too much dust on it. (It's) bad enough as it is.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Yeah. (Pause) About another 8 inches or so. That looks pretty good.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Is that about level?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Yeah. It looks pretty level to me, Al. Okay, the CPLEE's coming off. [Ed has reached 2+20 in his checklist.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: No, it's not (level). (Pause) Well, okay. We'll fix it up. When you get that baby (the CPLEE) off there. (Pause)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay, Houston. Al is reading 3.75; reading 55 on the O2. I have no flags; I'm on minimum cooling and very comfortable.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger, Al. Go ahead, Ed.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay, hold on here. (Pause) Okay. Ed is reading 3.75. Is reading 43 percent, and has no flags, is on minimum cooling, and feeling very comfortable.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger, Ed. (Pause) And for your information, Antares, those numbers compare very well with our predictions; and it looks like you're going right down the old line.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Very good.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: And just by way of reference, I show you about 38 minutes behind the nominal timeline at this point.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay. We'll give you a little credit for that, Bruce. Better make up your mind as a television technician. [Al is telling Houston that part of the 38 minutes was due to Houston's requests for fine-tuning of the TV pointing, zoom, and sensitivity. While Mitchell is deploying the CPLEE, Al is leveling and aligning the Central Station prior to releasing 16 Boyd bolts which will let the spring-loaded top of the Central Station pop up into place at about waist height, raising the thermal curtains in the process. Al has reached 2+14 in his checklist.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger. And, we're looking right now at about a 30-minute extension. I'll have more word for you on that later.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay. We'll keep plugging ahead, here. (Pause) Okay. I have just about the right amount of dirt. Central Station is level. (Long Pause) [The process of leveling the Central Station is a matter of moving dirt to raise a corner or of scraping dirt away to lower one.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay. Can you read, Ron?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay, Houston. The CPLEE is deployed. The (leveling indicator) ball is in the inner ring. And it is lined up due east. RealVideo Clip (4 min 19 sec)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger, Ed. [Each of the experiments has a gnomon, a short, vertical stick, which provides a shadow. Because the position of the Sun in the sky is well-known and changes only about a half degree per hour, it is possible to know ahead of time where the gnomon shadow should fall when the instrument is properly aligned. Ed is at 2+26 in his checklist.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: And we're going for the SIDE now.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: And it looks clean and pretty, doesn't it? That little CPLEE all sitting there.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: It won't (be clean) long.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: All trim and proper.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: You look very white, trim, and proper yourself. Little tarnished, now, but...

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Except for the lower extremities, huh? (Pause)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Ed, Houston. You confirm interim... (correcting himself) or initial mortar pack deployment.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: That's affirmative. I confirm it.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: It's lined up almost due north, Bruce, in order to have a free flight (of the grenades) away from all craters I can see and still miss the ridge that we're worried about.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Evans
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Kitty Hawk, Houston. In the blind, again. Time to start the camera.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger. We copy. (Pause)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay. Can you read, Ron?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Evans
a14a_1161107_pao.text: We just barely got you that time, Stu.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mission Control
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Stu aboard Kitty Hawk reported visual sighting of Antares at a GET of 114 hours 48 minutes.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mission Control
a14a_1161107_pao.text: This sighting occurred while in program 24, a computer program for landmark tracking. We're at 116 hours 37 minutes. 2 hours 18 minutes since cabin depress.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: (Moving toward the south) And I'm heading out with the SIDE and the CCIG at this point.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger. [Ed will deploy the SIDE/CCIG about 55 feet southeast of the Central Station, as indicated in the deployment sketch . Al is releasing Boyd bolts on the Central Station.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Say, Houston, relative to the CCIG, since we have these ridges to the south of us and this thing is being deployed somewhat in a hollow, is this going to upset the investigators?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Stand by. We'll get you an answer on that. (Pause)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: I don't really know what else we can do, since this whole area is a bowl.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Ed, you can go ahead and deploy in accordance with the nominal plans. We understand and that will not impact the experiment. (Pause) Ed, Houston. Do you copy deploy in accordance with the nominal plans? [Bruce is telling Ed that it's okay to deploy the experiment in the 'hollow' Ed described. In the meantime, Al has gone over to the MET. An enhanced frame from the 16mm movie shows him leaving the MET with what appears to be the tongs . Al does not tell us why he got the tongs, but one possibility comes to mind. At 117:30:24 in the A12LSJ, Al Bean talks about using Boyd-Bolt sleeves to weigh do

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay. Got you, Bruce. Thank you.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Sorry I was busy at that moment. (Long Pause as Ed begins to deploy the SIDE and Al returns to the Central Station)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay, Houston. To keep you honest, Al is operating on the Central Station at the moment. 116:36:53 McCandless: Roger, Honest Al. (Al Laughs) [Mitchell - "One of the problems with watching this on television at this point is remembering that we're operating with great magnification and, although it appears there's not much motion out there, all of the distances are foreshortened. And whereas we're moving 20 or 30 feet, it looks like we're only moving a few inches. It's hard to see our movement. And that's simply because of the long focal length of the lens."] [Jones - "And some contribution fro

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Evans
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Kitty Hawk, Houston. I guess remote site said that you were asking if we're picking you up, and - negative, we're not picking you up here.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay, up comes the Central Station. And that's one for the troops on the ground.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay. We're watching.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Can you actually see it from there?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: I couldn't see it move up. I can see something, so to speak, flapping in the breeze. I guess that's the foil (that is, the thermal curtains). RealVideo Clip (3 min 07 sec)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Flapping in the what? (Pause) [On Apollo 17, the Central Station sprang up into position and then the foil curtains shimmered for several seconds. Here, although the image is partly saturated, it appeared that the Central Station sprang up into position more slowly. Subsequent brightness variations are undoubtedly due to motions of the curtains.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Houston, I'm out here having a wrestling match with the SIDE and the CCIG. The SIDE is so light (and) the cable is sufficiently stiff that every time I touch the CCIG, it almost turns the SIDE over. It's turned it over twice on me, now. [Conrad and Bean had an identical problem with their SIDE/CCIG. The cable connecting the two pieces of equipment is very stiff and has some loops and kinks in it from the days or weeks that it has been stowed in the LM. Ed is having a tough time getting the CCIG into position and in the right orientation and, in the process, is having the CCIG "tail" disturb th

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Want some help up there, Ed?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger; standby...

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Well, give me another minute with it and I'll have it; I think.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Say again on that, Ed.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Say again?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Yeah, I missed your last.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: I said I've been wrestling with the SIDE and CCIG out here. And the cable is still sufficiently stiff, and the SIDE is sufficiently light - has sufficiently little mass - that it keeps getting tipped over.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Can you do anything by moving it back a little bit toward the Central Station to slack off the cable?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: No, no, no, no. It's the cable from the CCIG to the SIDE.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Evans
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Kitty Hawk, Houston in the blind. Coming up on T 1 time.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Oh, okay.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: A little hysteresis problem, huh? [In an engineering sense, hysteresis is literally a delayed reaction or a "retardation of effect". Here, Al is referring to the fact that the SIDE/CCIG has retained memory of the coiled state it was in for weeks prior to deployment.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: There it goes again. (Pause) Okay, Houston. I think I have it leveled. Besides that, it's poorly balanced, it turns out; it wants to tip over very easily to the rear. The CCIG is aligned and leveled. (Correcting himself) I mean the SIDE is aligned and leveled; and the corners, I guess I better check those.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay, Ed. If you have a problem, SIDE is first priority; CCIG comes second.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Rog. (Long Pause)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: It's interesting, Bruce, that the dynamics of the SIDE are such that (pause) just pulling this (dust cover) pin on it almost tipped it over again. I had to use a lever technique to get it off. RealVideo Clip (1 min 41 sec)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay. The SIDE is deployed.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger. And copy, the dust cover's off.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay. We'll head back (to the MET) and get on to the thumper geophone.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay. What's the status of the CCIG, Ed?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: (Moving west to the MET as he talks to McCandless) It's in good shape. It's deployed about 4 feet to the southeast (of the SIDE), and pointing almost due south with a little bit to the west.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Beautiful. (Long Pause) [Mitchell, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I had no particular problem getting the SIDE out to the site (55 feet/17 m southeast from the Central Station), after we finally got it off of the subpallet. It eventually ended up to the southeast, with the CCIG to the south as the photographs plainly show. However, it was really a hassle getting the SIDE and the CCIG deployed. The Number One problem was that the leg configuration on the SIDE is totally unstable in one-sixth g. The small mass of all of that equipment makes it so easy to turn over just by a touch. The cable

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Al, this is Houston. I show about 3 to 4 minutes overdue on the magazine on the 16-millimeter camera.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Since I'm heading over there, now, Al, I'll turn it off.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Okay. You shut it off, and we'll change the mag later. (Long Pause) RealVideo Clip (3 min 33 sec)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: (Now at the MET) Okay. (Pause) And Bruce, I'm going to go to Intermediate Cooling just for a few minutes. For a couple of minutes.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger, Ed. (Long Pause) [Jones - "Your decision to take a rest suggests that you were working pretty hard to get that SIDE/CCIG deployed. I presume that you were having to lean over against the suit pressure."] [Mitchell - "Yeah, it's an effort trying to move against the suit. And I had a personal policy that, if I felt myself starting to break a sweat - more than just break a sweat - I would go to intermediate cooling. I tried to operate my metabolic rate and the cooling such that I was right on the verge of breaking a sweat. And, if I really started to sweat I went to higher cooling and, if

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: I've got it in between Low and Intermediate, now. (Pause)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger, Ed. (Pause)

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: And I'm going to take penetrometer measurement, now, Houston.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: As I get ready for the thumper. (Long Pause) [Ed is at 2+36 in his cuff checklist and, since they are 3 hours 5 minutes, into the EVA, he is 30 minutes behind. Unlike Conrad and Bean on Apollo 12, he has deployed the SIDE/CCIG without a great loss of time. Al has just gone over to the subpallet to get the Central Station antenna mast. He is at 2+24 in his checklist.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Ooh, that new extension handle works well. [The extension handle flown on Apollos 14 to 17 had a length of 76 cm versus 61 cm on Apollos 11 and 12. The locking mechanism with which the handle was mated to tools was re-designed, as well.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Houston, I'm taking these measurements now at a site about 15, no, about 25 feet south of the Central...Not of the Central Station but of the RTG. And here goes my first one. One hand. (Pause) And Houston, I can push it in...Well, let's see; it's gone nearly all the way in.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Evans
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Kitty Hawk, Houston in the blind. You can start the camera.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1161107_pao.text: (Looking over at the penetrometer) Six marks. Six blacks showing.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Six. 1, 2, 3. 1, 2, 3. A double one and a black and white. A white, a black, and white below the upper double one. Do you understand?

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless
a14a_1161107_pao.text: Roger. We do.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: That's with one hand. (Pause) [Al has gone over to the subpallet to get the gimbal assembly heÕll use to aim the antenna. Ed's image is merged with that of the MET and the combination is too saturated to let us see anything of what he is doing.]

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1161107_pao.text: With two hands (pause), I can push it all the way in.

a14a_1161107_pao.speaker: McCandless

a14a_1344654.text: (At the foot of the ladder) Did you...I saw you over here. Did you get a picture (of Earth)?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: I did. Of the LM in the foreground?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Yeah.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Yep. Several.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, you ready to go up?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Sure! 135:24:38 Mitchell: All right, Fredo, I'm starting up the ladder.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Haise
a14a_1344654.text: Roger, Ed. [Al snags the TV cable and finally pulls it hard enough to pull the camera far enough forward over the tripod base that it falls to the ground, apparently without damage.]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: (Stomping his boots on the ladder) How's that doing?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: That's good. Shaking the heck out of the LM.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Huh?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Haise
a14a_1344654.text: Okay...

a14a_1344654.speaker: LM Crew
a14a_1344654.text: (Garbled)

a14a_1344654.speaker: Haise
a14a_1344654.text: ...someone must have got caught in the cable; we just saw the TV go over.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Well, we finally did it to you; sorry. [Jones - "Just a matter of arcane interest, when the camera falls over, it winds up with the horizon in the field-of-view, but there's quite a bit of dust on the lens."]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Haise
a14a_1344654.text: (Chuckles) Okay.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Want to take it up? I'll go set it...I'll go set it back up again. Get it?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Yeah.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay. (Exaggerated speech) Fix up the television camera. (Long Pause as Al rights the camera and uses a lens brush on it) Okay, Fredo, you're going to have a real practical problem here. Probably be able to see what the lunar dust does to a camera lens.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Haise
a14a_1344654.text: Okay.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Aim it back at the LM. Do you see anything at all?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Haise
a14a_1344654.text: Yeah. I think it's a better picture. Lunar dust helps the TV picture, I guess.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: (Laughs) Okay, we'll see to it that all TV lenses get dusted in the future. RealVideo Clip (3 min 10 sec)

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Cuts you down four stops, Fred.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Haise
a14a_1344654.text: Yeah, that looks... You just about had it centered, there. That's good, Al.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay. [Ed is back down on the footpad and, once Al has the camera aimed, Ed jumps up onto the ladder. It appears that he doesn't quite make the bottom rung, but scrambles up to it by using his feet on the strut.]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Did you see that mighty leap, Fredo? [Jones - "You're pulling with your arms?"] [Mitchell - "Yup."] [Jones - "You bend your knees a little bit."] [Mitchell - "Give a push and little pull at the same time and just float up and grab on. Actually, you launch yourself off the ground, guided by your hands and kind of grab onto the ladder as you go by the step you want."]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, Ed, you can start on up, now.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: I'm already halfway up.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, good show.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Rock box in one hand. [Mitchell, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I carried it up by myself from the ground level without any great problem at all. I just bounced up from the surface to the first rung with the rock box in my left hand."] [Encumbered with the rock box, Ed is stepping up the ladder, rather than jumping from rung to rung.] [As Al goes toward the MESA, he makes a football "cut" to his left to get around the MET. In two EVAs, he has developed a smooth, easy stride. Their heart rates are 108 (Al) and 114 (Ed). Figure 10-5 in the Apollo 14 Mission Report shows the crew's heart rate

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay. (Long Pause) How are you doing?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Fine. If I get some of my visors up here so I can see. (Pause as Ed hops part way down the ladder) How far back do I have to look (for Earth)?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: What for?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: (To) look up there.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Well, right about there. [Earth is almost exactly overhead. In the TV picture, we can see Ed lean back to his right, sticking his left leg out as he tries to get tilted far enough back to see Earth.]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Oh, I'm looking the wrong way. [Ed hops down another rung and leans way back to his left, far enough that his PLSS gets into sunlight.]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, shall we press on?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: One second. There it is.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: We got two loads of the ETB.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Okay. (Garbled) go.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: (Climbing up to the porch) Just had to have a quick look at Earth from the...

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Yeah.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: ...surface. [During the 1991 mission review, Ed and I thought he might have come down the ladder to get the ETB from Al. However, a close examination of the TV record indicates that he did not and just came down to look at Earth.]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Well, I got some pictures of the LM in the foreground; so, hope it comes out all right.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Reading me, Ed? Okay. Houston, do you read?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Pretty small sliver left, isn't it?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Yeah. Not much. (Long Pause)

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, why don't you take the first ETB as soon as you're ready; then, we can run the tracker light thing in between. (Pause; still at the MESA) Okay, standing by. You ready for it? (Pause) [Ed is getting into the cabin and getting himself in position to operate the LEC . Al is at the MESA attaching the ETB to the LEC hooks.]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Haise
a14a_1344654.text: Roger, Al. Houston reads you loud and clear.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: You reading me, Al?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Yeah. I read you. Yeah, I read you, Al...(correcting himself) Ed. [Al is moving toward the ladder with the ETB hanging from the LEC at helmet height.] RealVideo Clip (3 min 07 sec)

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, I'm ready to bring it up.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: (Moving into the LM shadow to get into position directly west of the ladder) Okay, stand by. I'm going to get around a little bit more, here. Okay, let her go. (Long Pause as the ETB goes up to the cabin) Very good. (Long Pause) [Al is standing just outside the north edge of the LM shadow, his upper body in sunlight, waiting for Ed to get the ETB off the LEC.]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Fredo, is the ALSEP antenna still doing okay?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Haise
a14a_1344654.text: Stand by Ed. Roger, Al; they're getting good signal.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, that's good. [Comm Break. Al stands waiting for a while and then goes over to the MESA for a few seconds before getting back into position west of the ladder. He gets there just as Ed calls down to him.] RealVideo Clip (3 min 38 sec)

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, Al, bring it (the ETB) down.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: (Pulling the LEC strap, hand over hand) All righty, coming back down. (Long Pause) Okay, hold it there.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Okay. [Once the ETB is over the porch lip, Al steps to his left, still pulling the strap, so that the ETB comes down on the MESA side of the ladder. He then moves closer to get the ETB.]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, I have it. (Taking the ETB over to the MESA and needing a little more strap) Little more...

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Huh?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: A little more down, please.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, you got it.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay. I've got it, now. Thank you. (Pause)

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay. Hook on there. (Garbled). (Pause) Open. (Long Pause as Al puts two weigh bags in the ETB) Okay, that (third weigh) bag is so big it won't go in the ETB very well; I'll just bring it up by myself.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Okay. You ready to bring the other two up?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Just a second. (Long Pause as Al closes the ETB and gets into position west of the ladder) Okay, you can take the strain now, if you like.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Okay. Here she comes. (Long Pause) [Mitchell - "The line was really sagging; and, to be hanging that way in lunar gravity, it had to be a pretty heavy bag."]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: (Releasing the LEC) Okay, it's all yours.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, I've got it.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: (Going to the MESA to get the remaining weigh bag) Don't I check the tracking light now, before I come up?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Yup. (Pause)

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Got your eye bones out of the way?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: I'm not looking at it. Let me know when you turn it around. (Pause) [Mitchell - "You can't look at the light when it comes on. It's a high intensity, flashing light and you don't want to look at it when it comes on. He turns around and then looks at it to see if it's flashing. But he doesn't want it to flash in his eyes unexpectedly."] [Jones - "So you look away, turn it on and then just kind of turn your head a little bit and do a peripheral check."]

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, (garbled). (Garbled) track light (circuit breaker) closed. Okay, here it comes. (Pause)

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay. Let's see. (going to the foot of the ladder and looking up) Yeah, track light's working.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. RealVideo Clip (3 min 10 sec)

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, Houston, crew of Antares is leaving Fra Mauro Base.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Haise
a14a_1344654.text: Roger, Al, you and Ed did a great job. Don't think I could have done any better myself.

a14a_1344654.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1344654.text: That's debatable, isn't it, Fredo?

a14a_1344654.speaker: Haise
a14a_1344654.text: Well, I guess not now, Ed. (Long Pause) [Fred Haise and Jim Lovell were supposed to have landed at Fra Mauro on Apollo 13. Because of an oxygen tank explosion during the journey to the Moon, their landing was scrubbed. Like the crews of Apollos 15, 16, and 17, Lovell and Haise had the advantage of having trained as backups to a landing mission (Apollo 11) and, therefore, were able to devote a far greater fraction of the their training time to geology than the crews of Apollo 11, 12, and 14 who, appropriately, devoted most of their training time to spacecraft systems and flight operations. Hais

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: Okay, the dust is knocked off (of his boots). (Long Pause as he steps up the ladder, one foot at a time)

a14a_1344654.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1344654.text: (Probably on the porch) How'd you like one more bag of rocks?

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. "Verify EVA circuit breaker configuration."

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Mine's good.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Okay, mine's good.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Suit Fan 2 (circuit breaker), Closed; Suit Fan Delta-P, Closed; ECS Caution and Water Sep Component lights " are not out. They're going out. Okay; they're out. (Garbled). Okay. We can doff gloves. (Long Pause)

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. Gloves are off. (Pause) "Stow on the comm panels. Verify the safety's on the dump valve ."

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Okay; it is. (Pause)

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Want "Descent Water valve, Open."

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay, Descent Water valve is open.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Okay.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. (Remove) purge valves .

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Let's see. Have we got...(Pause as Al double checks the checklist) Okay.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Pardon?

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Yeah. I was just rechecking, to be sure we had everything. (Pause) Okay. Purge valves. Stow in the purse .

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Okay.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: And disconnect the...

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: OPS O2 hose.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: OPS O2 hose. Somewhere.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Right there. (Pause) Okay.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. "Connect LM O2 hoses red to red and blue to blue." [Comm Break]

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: "(PLSS) Pump, Off; and the Fan, Off."

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Stand by one (moment), Ed. Will you verify this hose for me?

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. They're locked.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Okay, we want Suit Flow. Good.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Pump, Off; and (PLSS) Fan, Off.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Good. Pump, Off; PLSS Fan, Off. "Disconnect PLSS water from PGA." (Garbled). Okay.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. Here's your (LM) water (hose).

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: And "connect LM water to PGA". Where do you want to go? (Garbled) do the same (garbled). Okay. (Long Pause) [They may be working out the routing of the various hoses.]

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Get it?

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Yeah. Got that one. (Long Pause) It's a real bitch, isn't it? (Pause) Okay; got it. Okay; "close the LCG Pump breaker".

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: LCG Pump breaker is closed.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Kitty Hawk, Houston. How we doing?

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. PLSS mode, both, to O, and connect to the... [They are turning off the RCU and will be off comm until they connect to the LM comm system.]

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Howdy. Getting along real fine.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: (Garbled).

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Now wait a minute; do you...Both do it together.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Okay, Stu. We've got you this time, I think.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Yeah.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Both set up our (comm) panels alike.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Yeah.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: And, we'll talk and set it up (garbled).

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: Okay.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Okay?

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Going to O. [Comm Break]

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Yes. I'm reading you loud and clear.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Okay, Stu. We'd like to give the high gain a chance here to do its stuff with the Servo Electronics Power in Secondary. So what we'd like to have you do is go to Secondary with the High Gain Servo Electronics Power switch. Switch your - While your Track mode in Manual, set in a Pitch of minus 58, a Yaw of 185, and Beam Width to Wide. And then go into a normal acquisition, you know, trying to get it to Auto and then Medium and then down to Narrow. If for some reason that doesn't work, well then go on back to the way we've been - been doing it there in Manual, Medium, and Primary Electronics.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. Now, the Electronics are in Secondary now, Ron. They have been since yesterday.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Oh, okay. Well, why don't we press on anyhow and try a normal acquisition on the thing, then? Put your Pitch to minus 58, Yaw to 185.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Houston, Antares.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Haise
a14a_1354348.text: Go ahead, Antares.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: All right.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: And we'll see if it'll track in Auto at all, or if it'll - -

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Okay, we're on spacecraft comm now; and we're proceeding with the PLSS OPS undock...(correcting himself) undoffing, I should say.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. We'll give it a go.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Haise
a14a_1354348.text: Roger, Al. [Long Comm Break.] [They will remove the PLSSs, check to make sure that the OPSs are still working properly (in case they have to be used for an emergency spacewalk across to the Command Module), and prepare a jettison bag with unneeded equipment to be discarded along with the PLSSs. They perform the OPS check before discarding the PLSSs for the simple reason that, should one of the OPSs not check out properly, they will keep a PLSS. Astronaut Joe Engle, the backup LMP, takes over as CapCom.]

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: We got Narrow.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Well, how about that, sports fans! There's Auto and Narrow, good and solid.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Yes. It worked, looks like. Okay. Let's go ahead and leave it there, Stu. And let's see if it'll track when you start to maneuver to the COAS tracking attitude.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: And, Stu, for your information, Al and Ed are back at the LM. Al's down there hitting golf balls. Seeing how far he can hit them.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: How's that coming out?

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Al - looks like he had a couple of slices there, but then finally go - got a hold of one and really drove it down the old lunar surface.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Stu, you doing anything now? Do you want to talk about these normal docking procedures, changed there on page 52?

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. Just a second. Let me float out from under the couch here and get my book.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Okay.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. I'm on page 52.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Okay, Stu. Let me talk about it here a minute -for a little bit. As you know, normal procedures are we go whipping on in there, we get contact with the drogue, and then, as soon as we get capture, we go to CMC, Free. Well, the basic difference there is that we want the LM to do a little bit of thrusting. If for some reason, you know, it doesn't go to - the capture light, just don't capture, when you make contact. So, we just want you to press on in there, contact the drogue, and report contact to the LM. And then at that point, the LM is going to do a plus X, And, then as soon as you get captu

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: So at about 1 ? ?

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. Go ahead, Ron.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. Just to have it down in writing there, where it says translate to capture latch at about 144:07 or 08 in there somewhere, change that to, "translate to a contact with drogue."

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. "Translate to contact with drogue."

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: And then add, "report contact to the LM," immediately following that.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. I'll write that down. I'm sure I won't have to tell him.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: I don't think so either (laughing). But, that's his cue to go ahead and plus-X, if necessary, you know.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. I've got that - -

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Okay.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: - - Translate to contact with drogue, report contact to LM, and CMC, Free, at capture.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Yes. That's right. CMC, Free, at capture. The thing we didn't want to be is have you in CMC, Free, and the LM pushing against you, you know? In other words, don't go to CMC, Free, until you get capture.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Okay, that's done. And it sounds good to us. (Pause)

a14a_1354348.text: Okay. Can we press on now (with preparations for the depress and jettison)?

a14a_1354348.speaker: Engle

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Kitty Hawk, Houston. If you read, it's about 30 seconds from T-start time.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Engle
a14a_1354348.text: Okay, Al. We're watching that and it's looking good. Suits are looking good. (Long Pause) Okay, Antares. Could you verify Suit (Circuit) Relief (valve) in Auto, please? (Long Pause)

a14a_1354348.text: Okay, Houston. Suit Circuit Relief is now in Auto.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Engle
a14a_1354348.text: Okay; thank you, Al. [Comm Break] RealVideo Clip (2 min 41 sec)

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: Okay, Houston. We're going to jettison now.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Engle
a14a_1354348.text: Roger, Al. (Long Pause)

a14a_1354348.text: Houston, do you read Kitty Hawk?

a14a_1354348.speaker: Evans
a14a_1354348.text: Okay, Kitty Hawk. This is Houston. We?ve got you now.

a14a_1354348.text: Okay. Well, that should have been right on the target, Ron. And my frame counter is 87.

a14a_1354348.text: Roger. 87 on that one. And while I think about it, on page 35 there, we missed your percent remaining on the galactic survey and lunar libration -camera.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay. After the lunar libration, I'm reading 60 percent.

a14a_1354348.speaker: CC
a14a_1354348.text: Roger. 60 percent.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Engle
a14a_1354348.text: You guys really registered the seismometer on those last ones.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1354348.text: That's good. Good heavy throw. [In the video clip, we see three bulky items come out of the hatch, one at a time. The first impacts the surface in the LM shadow at 136:24:05 (13:27:07 GMT/UTC on 6 February 1971). This undoubtedly the Disposal Container. The second is one of the PLSS, which comes out one a flat trajectory at speed, emerges from the north side of the LM shadow and lands outside the TV field-of-view at about 136:24:43 (13:27:50 GMT/UTC). In a post-jettison photo Ed took out his window, AS14-66-9338 , this is the PLSS closest to the flag shadow. The final object to come out the ha

a14a_1354348.text: We're hoping you cleared the Velcro on those before you left.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1354348.text: That's affirmative. We got it. 136:26:06 Engle: Great. Thank you. [Mitchell - "I think what this is, is that Joe (Engle) and Gene (Cernan) put backup crew patches on the Velcro on the PLSS and they just wanted to make sure that we didn't throw them away." At the post-flight splashdown party, Shepard presented Gene Cernan with a display plaque featuring a back-up crew patch that was Velcroed to the back of Shepard PLSS during the EVAs. a14a_1354348.speaker: CC

a14a_1354348.text: Okay. Ron. Let me hold off for about 2 or 3 minutes, if you would, please.

a14a_1354348.speaker: CC
a14a_1354348.text: Okay.

a14a_1354348.speaker: CC
a14a_1354348.text: And then when you get there, we'll be giving you an update, and also I've got some P24 pads for you.

a14a_1354348.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1354348.text: Okay.

a14a_1354348.text: Antares, Houston.

a14a_1354348.text: Okay. We got quite a few things, I think, to stow here. We'll get with you and tell you where we're putting them.

a14a_1354348.text: Okay. Very good. [Very Long Comm Break. Fred Haise returns as CapCom.]
