a14a_1384237.text: You've got it.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1384237.text: Okay.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1384237.text: And how's our friendly Command Module Pilot doing? Is he going to be ready to pick us up with a nominal launch time? [Ron Evans, who has been Command Module CapCom during this shift, answers Shepard.]

a14a_1384237.speaker: Evans
a14a_1384237.text: You bet, Al, I've been talking with him all morning here, and he's really whipping around, getting a lot of pictures, and doing a lot of landmark tracking . He said he's picked you up on two passes now, and he also saw the reflections from the ALSEP on his last pass up through there.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1384237.text: Was he shooting sextant camera?

a14a_1384237.speaker: Evans
a14a_1384237.text: On one pass he was...

a14a_1384237.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1384237.text: Or just visual?

a14a_1384237.speaker: Evans
a14a_1384237.text: Just visual on this last pass, though.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1384237.text: Very good. How about the Hycon? Did he ever get that going?

a14a_1384237.speaker: Evans
a14a_1384237.text: That's negative.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1384237.text: That's too bad.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Evans
a14a_1384237.text: Yeah, that's right.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1384237.text: Yeah. Ron, the ALSEP, from the top of Cone Crater, is so bright, it stands out like a little jewel. I'm not surprised at all that Stu could see it.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Evans
a14a_1384237.text: He was really convinced that that's what he saw. And he didn't even know where it was, you know, and asked me where it was, and I came back, and sure enough confirmed it, and that's where it was.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1384237.text: That's very good. [Long Comm Break]

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Okay, Kitty Hawk. The lack of noise is music to my ears.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Okay.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: And - -

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Looks like you have a good lockup here.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Yes, It's working fine. And we?re standing by for your magazine percentage and also your P52.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Okay. The magazine percentage is 35.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Roger; 35.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: And, let me find my P52.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: And, the P52, if you're ready.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Ready to copy.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Okay. Minus 00.002, minus 00,166, minus 00.005; torque at 137:18:00.

a14a_1384237.text: Do you want to talk about your Noun 05 today?

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: I figured as much. Okay. We copy: minus .002, minus .166, and a minus .005; torque's at 137:18:00

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Roger. Hey, is Freddo still there?

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Yes, wait 1. He's talking to the "LMies" right now.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: No, that's all right - that's all right. I was just - you know, not only seeing the LM, I saw the Sun glinting off the ALSEP, I'm sure. And I was just wondering if it was deployed out by that crater at about CL 0.8 or 85/65.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Okay. I got a map here. Looks like it was about pretty close to CR and 63, is the ALSEP.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: C what?

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Charlie-Romeo and 63. It's really Charlie-Quebec 0.9 and about a 63.2.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Okay.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Where did you say you thought you saw a bright spot there?

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Well, now, I'm wondering if I got my direction from the LM - you can get the LM because it's by the Triplet.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Right.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: And, I just looked out and saw the bright spot going toward - parked out by another crater. And I'm thinking maybe I got my directions from the LM wrong. Is ALSEP out by that crater called Neighbor on the map?

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Wait a minute; I don't have Neighbor on this particular map I'm looking at. ALSEP is kind of between Doublet and Triplet, if you can see that part of it there. And, it's toward Doublet from the LM.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1384237.text: Houston, Antares.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Evans
a14a_1384237.text: Houston. Go.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Yes, well that's where I called - that's where I said the first time, and it didn't fit in. You told me Charlie-Quebec 0.9*

a14a_1384237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1384237.text: Hey, Ron. Tell them that this high gain antenna is setting here, kind of wobbling, and making all sorts of racket, when it should be setting very still and quiet, and was until just a minute or so ago. Now it seems to be starting to go unstable, or at least neutrally stable, and it's not driving wildly, but it's making a hell of a racket. It's just kind of wobbling, around a neutral point.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Wait 1, Stu, until I get the right - same map you're looking at.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Evans
a14a_1384237.text: Okay, INCO copies that, and we'll let you know on it. [Comm Break. Fred Haise returns as CapCom.]

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Okay. I was looking at a smaller map. It's got some more numbers in there. You're right. It's really right there by Neighbor, just east - just south of Neighbor. It's right in a line between the center crater of Triplet and Doublet.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Well, now, the coordinates that I called the first time just - you know, I didn't compare the map when I was looking through the sextant, but it looked to me like the - just judging on here, the ALSEP would be about CL 0.9 and right at 65, maybe 64.9. And, see, there's a little crater. See that little crater right there at about CL 8 and maybe 64 -64.5, or something like that.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Okay. Yes, I think that - I think that was the ALSEP --

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Yes, I think right there is - Yes. I can see the Sun shining off the beauty.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Yes. That was it; that was it.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Okay, Kitty Hawk there. Maybe we ought to whip into the update - map update or the flight-plan update for the next REV. And we'11 start out with the zero-phase pad backward on page 43.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Okay, Ron. Where we going to do - we going to have the first zero phase and then shoot Descartes?

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: And, Houston; Kitty Hawk.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Houston, go.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: That's affirm.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Okay. Sounds like a good idea.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Yes, it ought to be pretty good. And for the zero-phase backward PAD, roll angle is 195.4; pitch, 344.4; yaw, 359.9, T-start, 139:41:42. You write down your switch time - is 758. And, just a note...

a14a_1384237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1384237.text: Antares, Houston.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1384237.text: Go ahead.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1384237.text: Okay, they've made some configuration change on the ground station hookup down here to you; and for some reason, they think that that may have helped your antenna chatter, or whatever. The thing seem to be steadier now?

a14a_1384237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1384237.text: It steadied out for a minute or so, and now it's picking up again.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1384237.text: Okay.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1384237.text: Why don't they accept the fact that the damn thing is about to quit on us? (Pause) [Jones - "I think that may be the only time you ever got annoyed at the ground."] [Mitchell - "We were battling that damn antenna since we came around the Moon before landing. As I remember, we had trouble with that antenna in checkout. It exhibited some really strange patterns on the ground (at the Cape) before we left. I think that's why I'm exhibiting annoyance here, because we insisted that it be fixed. We thought it had been, and here we're on a lunar mission and we're having antenna problems."]

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Just a note there, Stu. When you start the DAC and stop the DAC, give a call so we can get a time hack on it.

a14a_1384237.text: Okay, Antares; Houston here. They'd like you to go back and select the lunar stay - the erectable.

a14a_1384237.text: Okay. 195.4, 344.4, 359.9, 139:41:42. Switch is 758, and I give you a mark for start and stop of the DAC on the camera.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Mitchell
a14a_1384237.text: Okay. [Very Long Comm Break. The following was scheduled to occur at the end of the eat period, nominally at 140:30 in transcript time. They are about an hour and a half ahead of schedule.]

a14a_1384237.text: Okay. Mighty fine. And, at the bottom of the page there on - at 140, add a Verb 49 maneuver. Verb 49 to a roll, 028; pitch, 253; and yaw, 0. That's to the COAS striking attitude.

a14a_1384237.text: Okay. 140, a Verb 49 to 028, 253, and 0 degrees.

a14a_1384237.text: Roger.

a14a_1384237.text: Okay. On page 44, got a little deletion there. Delete the Verb 49 at the top of the page, there. Say goodbye to Isadora and Compella; delete phototarget 7, there. And, in all that place in there, put the 500-millimeter procedures. And, at 140:15, put your T-start time of 140:15:13. And, then, you can go ahead and delete the zero-phase observations forward looking - which is kind of the rest of the page, there.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Roger. It looks like we?ll just delete everything else.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Yes, that's right. And the target point for that one is, as we mentioned before, you know about one and a third of those marks down the COAS, east of the depicted COAS position there.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Okay. I'll try to pick up that little Doublet there.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Okay.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Okay, Kitty Hawk. We got about 1 minute to LOS here. Al and Ed are completing a debriefing from their EVA. And I think they had - got about 160 pounds of stuff - 167 pounds of stuff coming back up to you.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: Jolly good.

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Roger.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Roosa
a14a_1384237.text: 160 pounds of rocks and a probe, huh?

a14a_1384237.speaker: CC
a14a_1384237.text: Yes. You betcha.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1384237.text: Houston, Antares; we have a crew's status report for you.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1384237.text: Okay, go ahead, Al.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Shepard
a14a_1384237.text: Okay, on the PRD (Personal Radiation Dosimeter): Commander, 16052; LMP, 7050. Negative medication; we're all in excellent health and excellent spirits.

a14a_1384237.speaker: Haise
a14a_1384237.text: Okay, Al, sounds great. [Other than Ed's annoyance over the antenna problem, "excellent spirits" is almost an understatement.] [Very Long Comm Break.] [Bruce McCandless takes over as CapCom for the launch.]
